====================================================================================================

Israel teaches students how to vote, but not how to make an informed political choice - opinion
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
08:52:05 UTC
17:52:05 KST

Many students in Israel will encounter an Education Ministry worksheet titled “Who should I vote for?” – a sensible question, indeed. Made accessible in a modern format through a QR code, it invites students to rank the qualities they want in a party and in a Knesset member.
A valuable exercise, no doubt, but it stops just short of where a young voter needs the most help.
How does a student discover which party actually reflects the priorities they identify as important? Where should they look for reliable information? How should they judge a promise against a party’s record, or decide between two plausible arguments?
The worksheet offers little guidance. It does not ask students to compare platforms, check promises against performance, evaluate the reliability of sources, identify manipulation, or weigh conflicting evidence. This format carries forward a gap that has existed in election education for years, and the same gap appears in the election materials we reviewed in an Israel Democracy Institute analysis ahead of the election for the 26th Knesset.
First-time voters will account for about 10 percent of Israel’s eligible electorate. For those still in school, election season may be one of the few chances to practice political judgment in a setting where learning comes first.
The public isn't entirely convinced. In an IDI public opinion survey conducted in July 2026, 27 percent of Israeli adults said they wanted schools to avoid election-related topics, 34 percent favored teaching only the formal process, and 33 percent supported open discussion of parties’ positions on major issues.
Education Ministry encourages mock elections, lessons on voting
Nonetheless, Israel's Ministry of Education has laid some useful groundwork, encouraging mock elections, discussion of civic participation and lessons on the importance of voting. Yet these efforts fall short of encouraging meaningful democratic participation, focusing on electoral procedure, with less attention paid to helping students develop well-informed political judgment.
Partisan campaigning is prohibited, rightfully so, and schools are expected to expose students to a range of positions. One way that students are exposed to these positions is by holding panels with representatives from political parties, a longstanding practice that illustrates both the promises and limits of the current system.
The Ministry sees these encounters as ways to expose students to a range of views and give them practical experience in democratic participation. But the Israeli public is divided on the value of such panels, especially across religious groups, whose members often attend separate school systems in Israel.
In an IDI public opinion survey conducted in July 2026, a small majority of secular Israelis (55%) said they support holding such panels, while a majority from all other religious subgroups, traditional, national religious, and Haredim, said they oppose such panels, with Haredi opposition the highest at 82%.
Moreover, the educational value of the panel depends on whether schools truly give students the opportunity to encounter a broad range of positions and whether they are given the tools to compare and assess what they’re hearing.
These tools are limited, as reflected in our review of the topics suggested for classroom discussion in the Ministry of Education’s election materials: “the economy,” “security,” “law,” “welfare,” and Israel as a “Jewish and democratic state.”
While these categories appear to invite political discussion, their broad and abstract framing largely strips away the concrete controversies that define electoral debate. The judiciary, for example, is subsumed under “law,” while Jewish-Arab relations do not appear among the suggested topics at all.
That is a serious gap because political choices are made through disagreement.
A student who says security is a top priority still has to choose among parties that may all claim to protect Israel while offering very different strategies. A student who cares about Israel’s Jewish and democratic character has to consider what those principles require when they come into tension.
The same is true of economic policy, the judiciary and relations between Jews and Arabs. Schools can help students work through those competing claims with evidence, context and an understanding of the tradeoffs involved, while remaining nonpartisan.
Teachers lack training, support for appropriate classes
Many teachers currently lack the training and institutional backing to lead that kind of conversation. They fear complaints from parents, administrators, and public figures if a lesson is perceived as political, and indeed, ministry guidance spells out restrictions in detail and gives far less attention to the practical work of running a balanced debate.
When the cost of a misstep feels high, and the guidance feels vague, silence and avoidance become the safest choice.
Controversial questions can be discussed in a nonpartisan classroom. The quality of the discussion depends on the sources chosen, the accuracy with which competing views are presented, the way unsupported claims are challenged and the teacher’s willingness to let students reach their own conclusions.
These are professional skills, and the ministry can set clear standards for them.
Schools also have something that campaigns and social media rarely offer: time and structure. A teacher can slow a claim down, ask where it comes from, put competing proposals side by side, and require students to understand an argument before dismissing it.
That kind of classroom work would give young voters practice separating slogans from evidence and strong opinions from well-supported ones.
Political literacy should become an explicit part of election education. Students need recurring practice with real sources and competing policy proposals. They should learn to trace a promise, examine a record in office, test a claim against evidence, explain an opposing position fairly, and reconsider a view when the facts change.
Israel’s schools already teach students that voting matters. The harder lesson is how to reach a decision worth owning.
The choice of which party to vote for is ultimately a personal one, but the capacity to make an informed and independent choice is part of the democratic civic competence that must be developed long before Election Day.
Meital Baron and Daphna Cahana-Dolev are experts at the Israel Democracy Institute's Education Policy Program.

K-Beauty’s Brazil Push Signals a New Type of Korean Diplomacy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
08:52:00 UTC
17:52:00 KST

During a state visit to Brazil in late July 2026, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung called for a deeper partnership between Brazil and South Korea built on the following three pillars: commercial aircraft, critical minerals, and K-Beauty. While the first two are familiar agenda items across modern strategic partnerships, the third is decidedly not. Cosmetics rarely share space with jet manufacturing and rare earths, and their place on Lee’s diplomatic agenda reveals a lot about the Korean beauty industry’s growing role in Seoul’s foreign policy calculus.
Lee’s comment came at a Korea-Brazil business roundtable in São Paulo on July 28, where alongside delegations from companies like Samsung and HD Hyundai, the CEOs of K-Beauty titans AmorePacific Holdings, APR, Goodai Global, and Silicon2 joined the trade delegation. Meanwhile, a separate two-day showcase titled “K-Beauty Glow Big in Brazil” ran alongside the summit to put beauty brands like Beauty of Joseon, d’Alba, Isntree, and Mixsoon before Brazilian retail buyers.
Alongside the presidential roundtable, a second official channel was unfolding over the same period. On July 27, First Vice Minister Roh Yong-seok of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups met Brazil’s cosmetics association ABIHPEC and the e-commerce giant Mercado Libre, where they agreed to pursue joint research and marketing that pairs Amazon’s natural ingredients with South Korean cosmetic technology. According to Roh, such a partnership could pave the way for cosmetics becoming “the world’s number one export item,” provided the industry keeps strengthening and diversifying its markets.
For all of this forward-looking ambition, K-Beauty’s entanglement with geopolitics is nothing new. When Seoul agreed in July 2016 to deploy the U.S. Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) system in order to counter North Korean missile threats, China retaliated by restricting tourism and banning imports of 19 Korean cosmetics, which dampened what had been K-Beauty’s dominant market. The industry has spent the years since deliberately reducing its China exposure, and AmorePacific, the country’s largest cosmetics company, has publicly committed to rebalancing its China-heavy portfolio toward the West. Brazil is the clearest measure of how far this diversification now reaches. It is Latin America’s largest consumer market and the world’s third-largest beauty market after the United States and China, but historically it had drawn little Korean investment, mostly due to distance.
The recent increase in attention could be explained by trade statistics. Korea’s cosmetics exports to Brazil jumped more than tenfold in five years, from $5.17 million in 2020 to $54.36 million in 2025, according to Korea Customs Service data. Meanwhile, in the first half of 2026, cosmetics exports to Latin America by Korean small and mid-sized companies rose 131.9 percent while exports to Brazil alone surged 237.4 percent, making it the standout market even within a booming region. As one Silicon2 official noted, exports to the region “have just crossed $200 million, and the market is growing fast.”
Developing this opportunity has not been left solely to the K-Beauty companies, as the South Korean state has built a track for growth that predates Lee’s July visit. During a February 2026 summit between Lee and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and Brazil’s health regulator ANVISA signed a revised memorandum of understanding extending their regulatory cooperation to cosmetics for the first time, covering areas like e-labeling that determine how easily Korean products clear the border. That same visit also carried a lighter kind of diplomacy, when Lula, who has publicly credited Korean cosmetics for his own good looks, went home from Seoul with skincare from LG H&H and AmorePacific. Meanwhile, Lee used the occasion to promise Brazilian consumers that K-Beauty “will become even more accessible.”
K-Beauty has long been filed under soft power, a pleasant byproduct of the same Korean wave that carried K-pop and K-dramas abroad. However, it has since become a serious economic engine in its own right. Cosmetics generated a trade surplus of more than $10 billion in 2025, or roughly 12.9 percent of South Korea’s entire $78 billion surplus. The Brazil visit further demonstrates how the industry’s soft power is transforming into a commercial asset that the government now negotiates for and regulates around. K-Beauty has become an arena where the two forms of power feed into each other, where cultural influence built a demand that diplomacy is now converting into strategic and economic opportunities.
For the moment, however, the result of these dialogues resemble a buildup of momentum rather than any signed cosmetic deals. Lee and Lula agreed to push for a restart of stalled Korea-Mercosur trade talks with an eye on the December Mercosur summit, and Lula reportedly stated that the two countries “must double bilateral trade within two years.” Meanwhile, Seoul’s presidential policy chief, Kim Yong-beom, singled out cosmetics as an area where he expects substantial progress. None of this amounts to a treaty, but the overall direction is unmistakable.
Brazil is emblematic of what makes K-Beauty such a useful diplomatic instrument. The industry has proven adaptable, pivoting from a China dependency to U.S. and now Latin American markets in under a decade. It travels across very different consumer cultures, and its appeal has proven to have real staying power rather than fading with a single trend cycle. If the K-Beauty diplomatic experiment works anywhere, Brazil is where it will be proven, and Latin America is where the next chapter of Korean soft-power exports is most likely to be written.
This article was originally published on New Perspectives on Asia from the Center for Strategic and International Studies and is reprinted with permission.

The new British government plans to announce in the coming weeks a comprehensive package of economic sanctions and other measures designed to prevent the Israeli expansion of West Bank settlements.
Overall, the UK needs “a comprehensive reset of our policy” when it comes to the West Bank, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told the House of Commons on Tuesday. He spoke during his first question-and-answer session with lawmakers since he and the government he represents were sworn into office in July.
Miliband added that the new measures would include a ban on goods produced in the settlements and targeted sanctions on British institutions and individuals.
“We are looking, indeed, at our wider economic relationship with the occupied territories, and the different tools we have to tackle it,” Miliband explained. “We do not want British companies financing, constructing, or advertising new settlements. The work we are now undertaking is how we can stop that.”
Sa'ar warns of potential Israeli retaliation
Israel’s Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar warned Tuesday that if the UK acted against his country, the Jewish state would take retaliatory steps against Great Britain.
“We are prepared, and I hope they will not make the mistake of doing this. If they do, there will be a reaction,” Sa’ar said in a podcast interview with the Hebrew news website Ynet.
Tensions between Israel and the UK have been escalating in light of Israeli military actions in Gaza and the West Bank following the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack.
The UK’s decision under the last government to recognize Palestinian statehood in 2025 inflamed the situation, which is expected to get worse should Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu win the October 27 election in Israel.
Any government that Netanyahu forms is expected to be right-wing and to continue the policies of the existing government, just as the UK under Miliband and the new Labour prime minister, Andy Burnham, are more willing than their predecessors to go head-to-head with Israel on the issue.
Miliband already floated the idea of targeted sanctions after Israel’s Lands Authority opened bids for 1,234 homes in the largely underdeveloped E1 section of the West Bank settlement of Ma’aleh Adumim in August, a move that he said would undermine any two-state solution to the Israel-Palestinian conflict.
Miliband went further on Tuesday when fielding a number of questions from lawmakers frustrated about the lack of UK response to Israeli actions in the West Bank, such as terror activity by Israelis against Palestinian civilians and continued settler building. This includes the opening of E1 bids last month.
The foreign secretary explained that his words reflected the policies Burnham had considered even before he entered Downing Street in July, such as a ban on trade for goods produced in the settlements. “We are obviously working across government and with our allies on these measures,” Miliband said.
Israel has said that it has a right to build settler homes in Area C of the West Bank, which is under Israeli military and civilian control and where all the settlements are located. Under the Oslo Accords, the West Bank was divided into three areas, with sections A and B under the auspices of the Palestinian Authority.
ICJ issued advisory against construction in Area C
The International Court of Justice in 2024 issued an advisory opinion explaining that such construction in Area C is illegal, affirming a long-held stance of the UN and many nations, including the UK
Concern has been particularly high with regard to the E1 project, which would add 3,400 homes to the municipal boundaries of the city of Ma’aleh Adumim by building on an underdeveloped hilltop. The Palestinian Authority and the international community, including past US administrations, have warned that the project would block contiguous Palestinian development in that area and thus make a Palestinian state untenable.
Miliband referenced that viewpoint when speaking to the House of Commons on Tuesday, explaining that E1 development had long been considered a “red line,” because the project “cuts through the heart of the West Bank and risks making a Palestinian state unviable.”
He affirmed the UK’s commitment to a two-state resolution, explaining that his government would not stand idly by while that vision was being destroyed by Israeli actions on the ground in the West Bank.
In a harshly worded attack on the UK and Miliband in August, Sa’ar on X warned that the UK’s statements on Israel were fueling antisemitism in Great Britain and emphasized that the Jewish people had a right to build anywhere in their ancestral homeland.

Australian researchers create floating titanium metamaterial
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
08:42:40 UTC
17:42:40 KST

- RMIT-led researchers built a 3D-printed titanium lattice that floats and stays buoyant even after significant structural damage.
- The material was 70% stronger than stainless steel or high-density plastic used in marine infrastructure at the same density.
Australian researchers have built a 3D-printed titanium structure that floats in water and keeps floating even after significant damage, according to a study led by RMIT University.
The material is a lattice made of hollow, interconnected titanium struts filled with polyurethane foam. Researchers said it withstands seawater exposure and is stronger than the stainless steel or high-density plastic currently used in jetties, buoys and floating sensors.
“Although metallic lattices can be incredibly light, with densities less than one-tenth the density of water, their open, interconnected spaces allow water to enter, causing them to sink,” said Dr. Jordan Noronha, lead researcher at RMIT’s Centre for Additive Manufacturing. “This has made these strong, lightweight structures unsuitable for marine infrastructure, until now.”
“By filling only the hollow titanium struts with polyurethane foam, we created a structure that allows water to flow through it while remaining buoyant even after significant cracking and damage,” Noronha said.
The researchers said the work is the first reported demonstration of a floating metal-hybrid lattice metamaterial. Samples floated in freshwater for more than two months during testing, according to the study.
To design the structure, the team introduced a measurement they call skeletal density. Conventional density calculations count all the open space inside a lattice, including space that water can fill and that therefore does not help the structure float. Skeletal density instead counts only the titanium walls and the sealed, foam-filled channels, the parts of the structure water cannot enter.
“This gives engineers a simple design rule: if the skeletal density is lower than that of the surrounding liquid, the structure will float, even when water flows through all its external openings,” Noronha said.
In compression testing, the titanium structure was 70% stronger than stainless steel or high-density polyethylene at the same overall density, the researchers said. In a two-week corrosion test using seawater from Melbourne’s Port Phillip Bay, the lattice lost 0.15% of its mass and less than 1% of its strength.
The structure also kept floating after damage that included cracking, failure at connection points and the fracture of an entire lattice layer, according to the study. It sank only after being severely crushed and compacted.
“Tiny, sealed cells in the foam trap gas and prevent water from flooding the hollow struts,” Noronha said. “In this way the foam acts as a distributed barrier that helps the structure remain afloat after damage, unlike conventional hollow marine structures, which can rapidly fill with water after cracking.”
The team built a 3D-printed marine buoy to test the concept and placed it in a turbulent seawater tank, rotating it up to 45 degrees. The researchers said the buoy remained stable without a sealed casing, protective coating or added flotation.
Project leader Distinguished Professor Ma Qian said the next steps include scaling up the demonstration parts and testing long-term performance under realistic marine and deep-sea conditions. Qian said the structure’s properties can be tailored by changing the material inside the titanium framework, opening potential uses beyond marine infrastructure in areas such as energy absorption, thermal management and vibration control.
RMIT’s Centre for Additive Manufacturing led the project with the Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers in France. The Australian Research Council and RMIT’s School of Engineering supported the research.
The study, “Breaking the surface: buoyant metal-polymer open-cell hybrid lattice metamaterials,” was published in the journal Advanced Materials.

West trying to draw India into ‘games’ against China – Lavrov
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03

17:42:23 KST

West trying to draw India into ‘games’ against China – Lavrov
Western countries are trying to draw India into a confrontation with China by pushing a more military role for the Quad grouping, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said at the Eastern Economic Forum (EEF) in Vladivostok. 
Lavrov said India feels “very uncomfortable” in the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) grouping, arguing that the US and Japan have sought to add a military component to it. 
“They are conducting maritime security exercises and are keen to draw our Indian friends into games against another great friend of ours – the People’s Republic of China,” Lavrov said.
The Quad grouping of India, the US, Japan, and Australia focuses on cooperation in the Indo-Pacific. Its activities cover areas ranging from trade and critical technologies to maritime security, with the four countries also taking part in the annual Malabar naval exercise.
At a meeting hosted by India in May, Quad foreign ministers launched a maritime surveillance initiative aimed at increasing information sharing and maritime domain awareness. India is also due to host the grouping’s next Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission, intended to improve interoperability and knowledge-sharing.
📹 Germany Wants To Be Europe’s Top Military Force ‘Again’... Lavrov Points To Nazi Past, Calls It ‘Extremely Dangerous’

Lavrov linked the grouping to what he described as a broader Western effort to weaken the central role of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) by creating smaller blocs in the region.
He said Western countries are also trying to establish a “second Quad,” comprising the US, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines – instead of India – with the aim of fragmenting ASEAN unity.
The four countries already cooperate in a separate defense format, sometimes referred to as the SQUAD. Their defense ministers agreed last year to deepen maritime and air activities and strengthen what they described as regional deterrence and response capabilities.
Lavrov has raised similar concerns before. In May last year, he accused NATO of trying to draw India into ”anti-China intrigues,” while calling for the revival of the Russia-India-China (RIC) trilateral format.
India has pushed back against suggestions that participation in the Quad is directed against Beijing, saying it pursues an independent foreign policy based on national interests.
Lavrov also accused NATO of seeking to expand its presence and infrastructure in Asia. The US-led military bloc has stepped up cooperation with Australia, Japan, South Korea, and New Zealand in areas including maritime security, cyber defense, and emerging technologies.

China outlines new five-year plan for sports powerhouse drive
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
16:41:16 CST
17:41:16 KST

The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on building a leading sports nation during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Xu)
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- China aims to expand its sports industry to more than seven trillion yuan (1.04 trillion U.S. dollars) by 2030 as part of a new five-year plan to build the country into a sports powerhouse, officials said Thursday.
The 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), approved by the State Council in July, also targets increasing per capita sports venue space to about four square meters and raising the proportion of residents who regularly exercise to around 40 percent, General Administration of Sport director Gao Zhidan told a State Council Information Office briefing.
Gao said the "Year of Deepening Governance" campaign rolled out earlier this year will tackle bottlenecks in the development of the sports industry. This includes sustained efforts to root out corruption, combat "toxic fan culture" and build a well-regulated sports governance system.
In elite sports, Gao said China will shift from a "prioritized breakthrough" strategy to a "comprehensive development" model centered on the "633" project. The initiative calls for consolidating China's strengths in six traditionally successful sports, including diving and gymnastics, developing three foundational sports comprising athletics, swimming and water sports, and revitalizing basketball, volleyball and football.
Zhang Xin, director of the administration's Competitive Sports Department, said authorities will make greater use of market mechanisms to develop elite sports by allowing enterprises, universities and social organizations to play a larger role in training and competition, while attracting talent, capital and technology from a wider range of sources.
Chen Xingnian, director of the Mass Sports Department, said the national fitness plan for 2026-2030 will focus on making services more targeted, inclusive, intelligent, integrated and better regulated.
More than 5,000 small-scale fitness facilities, including micro-sports parks and multipurpose courts, will be built or upgraded over the five-year period, with resources prioritized for densely populated areas where demand is greatest.
On the sports industry, Yang Xuedong, director of the Sports Economy Department, said the administration will streamline event approval procedures to reduce costs and improve spectator experiences while developing 100 high-quality outdoor sports destinations.
New technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, will be used to develop smart fitness services and virtual sports, Yang said.
Gao also reviewed China's progress during the 14th Five-Year Plan period, saying public fitness had become increasingly popular, Chinese athletes delivered the country's best overseas Olympic performance at Paris 2024 and the sports industry maintained strong growth.
"We have successfully forged a path to building a sports powerhouse with Chinese characteristics," Gao said. ■

Malta government seeks to calm tensions after acquittal in journalist murder trial

Acquittal in journalist murder trial stirs tensions in Malta
VALLETTA, Sept 3 - Malta's government has urged calm after the acquittal of a businessman accused of commissioning the 2017 murder of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.
The 53-year-old journalist and anti-corruption activist was killed in a car bomb attack outside her home in October 2017. Her murder set off a political firestorm in Malta as well as focusing international attention on its police and judiciary.
The verdict in her murder trial, delivered late on Wednesday, has angered the victim's family, and drawn criticism from press freedom group Reporters Without Borders, which said it was "beyond outraged" by the acquittal.
Roberta Metsola, the president of the European Parliament and a former Maltese politician, pledged to continue the fight for justice.
"When they assassinated you, in broad daylight, outside your family home, we promised that we would not let them sweep it under the carpet," she wrote in a Facebook post addressed to "Dear Daphne".
"That promise holds today. We will not give up and we will not give in," she added.
Prime Minister Robert Abela, returned to power in May, did not comment directly but his government urged restraint in a statement issued late on Wednesday.
"At this sensitive moment, the government appeals for prudence in public comments that could do more harm than good," it said in a statement.
Three men have been convicted of carrying out the killing and two others for supplying the bomb after earlier trials and are now serving lengthy jail sentences.
However, businessman Yorgen Fenech, heir to a property empire that includes hotels and casinos, was acquitted on Wednesday by an 8-1 jury vote on charges of complicity in murder and the lesser charge of criminal association to commit murder.
TRIAL EVIDENCE TO BE ASSESSED
Prosecutors cannot appeal the verdict, except in exceptional circumstances involving points of law.
Judge Edwina Grima, who presided over the trial, has ordered that evidence be sent to the Police Commissioner to determine whether third parties should face criminal proceedings.
During a trial that began in July, the prosecution had alleged that Fenech wanted Caruana Galizia dead because she was about to reveal information about him.
In his defence, Fenech accused Keith Schembri, who served as chief of staff to former prime minister Joseph Muscat, of being behind the murder plot – an allegation Schembri denies.
Caruana Galizia's son Matthew expressed dismay, writing on Facebook: "Terrible decision by the jurors that our country may never recover from. They had a great responsibility to deliver justice. And washed their hands of it."
The opposition Nationalist Party held a "silent demonstration" outside Abela's office overnight, during which party leader Alex Borg called for a recall of parliament from its summer break. REUTERS

China tightens border checks against polioviruses
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
16:41:04 CST
17:41:04 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- China's customs authority has rolled out enhanced screening and quarantine measures for travelers and goods arriving from polio-affected countries or regions.
The measures were announced after the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that the risk of international poliovirus spread remains a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
Effective from Thursday, travelers from polio-affected countries who have been in contact with polio cases or display symptoms such as fever, sore throat, cough, vomiting, diarrhea, neck stiffness, limb pain or flaccid paralysis are required to proactively declare their condition to customs upon entry, the General Administration of Customs said in a statement.
The administration also ordered sanitation treatment for inbound vehicles, containers, goods, luggage, and parcels that are, or may be, contaminated if they originate from polio-affected countries or regions.
The measures will remain in effect for one year and will also apply to any additional countries or regions that the WHO may designate as polio-affected during this period. ■

LISBON, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- The CAE-PAE Forum on Marine Technology and Ocean Engineering was held here on Wednesday, bringing together experts and scholars from the Chinese Academy of Engineering (CAE), the Portuguese Academy of Engineering (PAE) and the marine sector to discuss China-Portugal cooperation in marine technology and ocean engineering.
The forum featured discussions on marine engineering, maritime transport, shipbuilding and port engineering, with a focus on technological innovation in marine engineering and the sustainable use of marine resources.
Participants exchanged views on technological development and cooperation prospects in areas including marine engineering equipment, intelligent shipping, green ships, smart ports and marine renewable energy.
Experts and scholars from the two countries shared research findings and practical experience and explored ways to strengthen joint research and the commercialization of technological achievements.
During the forum, the CAE and the PAE also signed a memorandum of understanding on cooperation, marking a new stage of institutionalized cooperation between the two academies.
Sebastiao de Azevedo, president of the PAE, said the signing of the memorandum marked an important milestone in the China-Portugal cooperation in science, technology and engineering. It will further promote long-term cooperation between the two leading academic institutions, facilitate exchanges among researchers, experts and industry, and inject new impetus into China-Portugal cooperation in marine technology.
Chen Jianfeng, vice president of the CAE, said China and Portugal have achieved fruitful results in cooperation in marine science and technology, the blue economy and marine governance.
He called on the two sides to focus on frontier areas such as marine engineering, intelligent shipping and green ships, strengthen joint research and the commercialization of technological achievements, and promote high-quality development of the maritime economies of both countries.
He also called for greater cooperation on global issues including marine ecological conservation and the blue economy, to contribute China-Portugal expertise and solutions to global marine sustainable development.
Yang Yirui, Chinese ambassador to Portugal, said in a video address that Portugal was the first Western European country to sign a memorandum of understanding with China on jointly building the Belt and Road and the first EU member to officially establish a Blue Partnership with China.
Over the years, China and Portugal have continuously deepened cooperation in the maritime field, jointly establishing a number of high-level research platforms and achieving numerous practical results. Marine cooperation has become an important part of bilateral cooperation, Yang said.
He noted that the forum brought together leading academicians and experts in marine engineering as well as industry leaders, and would give a strong boost to the cooperation between the two sides in the maritime sector.
He expressed hope that the two sides would take the event as an opportunity to continue building high-level platforms for exchanges and inject fresh impetus into the China-Portugal Blue Partnership.
Carlos Guedes Soares, winner of China's International Science and Technology Cooperation Award in 2025 and an academician of the PAE, said he has been involved in China-Portugal cooperation in the maritime field for more than three decades and has witnessed mutually beneficial cooperation between the two countries.
Both China and Portugal attach great importance to the development of the maritime sector and related technologies, he said, adding that the forum provided an important opportunity for the two leading academic institutions to strengthen their links and launch bilateral cooperation.
He expressed hope that the event would help Chinese experts gain a better understanding of Portugal's research and industrial resources in the maritime field, and promote exchanges and cooperation in traditional maritime transport, the blue economy, marine resource development and renewable energy, laying a foundation for further cooperation and development. ■

Singapore employers remain cautious on wages, hiring despite improved outlook
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
16:40:38 CST
17:40:38 KST

SINGAPORE, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- Singapore employers are expected to maintain a cautious approach towards wage increases and hiring in 2027, even as the business outlook has improved modestly, a survey conducted by the Singapore National Employers Federation revealed on Thursday.
The Survey on Wage and Employment Outlook 2026/2027 found that rising manpower costs remained employers' biggest workforce challenge, cited by 83 percent of respondents, up from 79 percent in 2025.
Concerns over the rising cost of upskilling and reskilling workers also increased, with 30 percent of employers highlighting the issue, compared with 23 percent a year earlier.
However, labor market tightness has eased. Fewer companies reported difficulties attracting and retaining professionals, managers, executives and technicians, at 41 percent, compared with 47 percent previously. Concerns over shortages of local high-skilled talent also fell to 35 percent from 42 percent.
Despite the easing, attracting suitable talent remained employers' top human resource priority, cited by 59 percent of respondents. Companies are also placing greater emphasis on exploring and adopting artificial intelligence, with 48 percent identifying this as a priority for 2027, up from 39 percent for 2026, alongside efforts to upskill and reskill employees.
The survey showed a modest improvement in business sentiment, with the proportion of employers expecting uncertain prospects in 2027 falling to 63 percent from 72 percent in 2026. Meanwhile, 65 percent of companies expect to perform well, compared with 63 percent a year earlier.
The outlook, however, remains uneven across sectors. While some export-oriented industries are benefiting from stronger external and technology-driven demand, domestically focused sectors such as retail trade and food and beverage services continue to face softer consumer demand and rising operating costs.
The survey, conducted between June and August 2026, gathered responses from more than 300 companies employing close to 160,000 workers across 20 industries. ■

NEW DELHI: India and Belgium on Thursday signed a series of MoUs and agreements aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation across renewable energy, defence, trade, investment, maritime affairs, critical minerals, semiconductors and research, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever held talks in New Delhi.The agreements were exchanged in the presence of PM Modi and De Wever at Hyderabad House, with the two sides seeking to turn the longstanding India-Belgium relationship into a broader strategic and economic partnership.PM Modi said the two countries had agreed to strengthen cooperation in several emerging areas, including startups, maritime capacity building, universities and research, while also working towards a Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement to facilitate the movement of talent."Today, we agreed to strengthen connections between our startups and enhance capacity building in the maritime sector. We will also reinforce cooperation in the university and research sectors, and we will soon sign a Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement to facilitate the movement of talent. Today we also held detailed discussions on regional and global developments. Both India and Belgium believe in the rule of law, dialogue, and diplomacy.
.."The Prime Minister also highlighted the renewable energy MoU signed during the visit, saying it would provide fresh momentum to bilateral cooperation on sustainability. The two countries have additionally decided to enhance cooperation in the processing and recycling of critical minerals."Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we have agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries. Agreements reached between our governments and defence industries will open up new opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation against crime between our respective agencies. A clean energy future and reliable supply chains are our shared priorities. The MoU on renewable energy signed today will give new momentum to our cooperation on sustainability. We have decided to enhance cooperation in the processing and recycling of critical minerals. Belgium's expertise in semiconductors and India's scale complement each other; in this regard, we will work together to integrate Belgium's IMEC Institute with India's semiconductor ecosystem. People-to-people ties are the greatest strength of our relationship."
The two sides also discussed ways to strengthen economic ties following the conclusion of the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement earlier this year. PM Modi said India and Belgium had taken several steps to translate the opportunities created by the agreement into concrete economic outcomes."Earlier this year, we concluded a historic Free Trade Agreement between India and the European Union. This unprecedented cooperation between two of the world's largest democratic powers will further strengthen global stability, growth, and shared prosperity. India's sustained economic progress and this agreement have opened up new possibilities for our economic ties. Today, we have taken several significant steps to translate these possibilities into concrete results. We have established an 'Investment Fast-Track Mechanism' in India for Belgian companies. We have decided to make the India-Belgium Business Forum a regular mechanism. We will enhance synergy between the financial, fintech, and regulatory institutions of both nations, and through these measures, we will realize the goal of doubling bilateral trade over the next five years"
Defence cooperation emerged as another key component of the agreements and discussions. PM Modi said India and Belgium had agreed to increase military exchanges and training, while government and defence industry agreements would create opportunities for co-development and co-production of defence equipment.He also said the two countries would strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between their agencies to combat crime.PM Modi said India and Belgium were also working together on modern defence equipment and cited the Zorawar tank as an example of the expanding partnership."I had the opportunity to visit Belgium ten years ago, and I am delighted to see the remarkable progress our partnership has made over the past decade. Today, the scope of our cooperation has expanded beyond traditional sectors to encompass strategic areas such as defense and clean energy. We are collaborating on modern defence equipment, such as the Zorawar tank. We are also developing one of the world's largest green ammonia projects in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh."
On clean energy and technology, PM Modi said the renewable energy agreement would strengthen cooperation on sustainability, while the proposed integration of Belgium's IMEC Institute with India's semiconductor ecosystem would combine Belgian expertise with India's scale.The two countries also discussed critical minerals, particularly their processing and recycling, as both sides look to build more reliable supply chains.PM Modi said the latest agreements marked an expansion of ties beyond traditional areas such as diamonds and trade."Last month, Belgium and the Netherlands jointly hosted the Hockey World Cup. I extend my heartiest congratulations to you for the magnificent organization of this World Cup. I also commend our players for their hard work and performance. Diamonds have long linked India and Belgium. Today, we are transforming this historic bond into a comprehensive partnership. I am confident that our discussions today mark the beginning of a new chapter in our bilateral relations..."
The Prime Minister also placed the bilateral engagement in the context of ongoing global conflicts and geopolitical uncertainty, saying India and Belgium supported efforts towards peace while sharing a commitment to combating terrorism."... Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts towards an early end to conflict and the establishment of peace; furthermore, eradicating terrorism in all its forms is our shared commitment. Last month, Belgium and the Netherlands jointly hosted the Hockey World Cup. I extend my heartiest congratulations to you for the magnificent organization of this World Cup. I also commend our players for their hard work and performance. Diamonds have long linked India and Belgium. Today, we are transforming this historic bond into a comprehensive partnership. I am confident that our discussions today mark the beginning of a new chapter in our bilateral relations..."
PM Modi said the broader global environment remained challenging, with conflicts affecting food and fuel security as well as supply chains. He said India's economy had continued to maintain its momentum despite the uncertainty."The world is currently going through a period of great upheaval. Conflict situations persist in various parts of the globe, and uncertainty is impacting sectors ranging from food and fuel to supply chains. Even amidst this challenging environment, the Indian economy has maintained its momentum; we recorded a growth rate of 7.8% in the last quarter. Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world."
The agreements and discussions came during De Wever's first visit to India as Belgian Prime Minister. He is in the country from September 2 to 4 at the invitation of PM Modi. His visit is also the first by a Belgian Prime Minister to India in two decades.De Wever, who took office in February 2025, is accompanied by Belgium's Minister of Defence and Foreign Trade, Theo Francken, along with a high-level delegation of officials and business leaders, including representatives from the Belgian defence industry.Earlier on Thursday, Francken held the India-Belgium Defence Ministers' Meeting with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, where both sides discussed expanding defence cooperation and greater engagement between their defence industries."The world is witnessing a time of great geopolitical and economic turmoil. Most of it is not our doing, but we have to handle the challenges. In such situations, meeting a friend and partner like you provides a useful opportunity to exchange views and perspectives," Singh said.Singh said the recently held India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue had provided a framework for taking the bilateral partnership forward, particularly in defence and security."We welcome greater cooperation with Belgian and Indian defence companies," he said.Francken, meanwhile, called for deeper cooperation with India, highlighting the country's technological capabilities and saying Belgium needed partners such as India for future projects."We can learn so much from you. You are a high-technology country. You are one of the most densely populated countries, and we really need to work together because Belgium is an old Western European country with a lot of technology, but we need countries like India. We need to collaborate on future projects, and for Belgium, this is the way forward"Francken also referred to Belgium's economic mission to India led by Princess Astrid in March 2025, describing it as a first step towards a renewed relationship between the two countries.He said the mission had helped generate momentum in bilateral ties, with contracts being signed on collaboration projects within 18 months."That is amazing. This means that we worked hard, that our people worked hard, and that we can go further in this pathway."The Belgian minister also said De Wever's visit had a packed agenda focused on expanding bilateral cooperation."I'm very happy to be here with our Prime Minister. For first time in more than 20 years a Belgian Prime Minister is visiting your beautiful country. We have a busy, busy schedule with lot of signing ceremonies, a lot of good talks with the Prime Minister…"Francken said Belgium and India could address the geopolitical challenges facing the world through greater friendship and partnership."I think it's totally right when you talk about geopolitical challenges that we have to meet. We didn't organise them, we didn't always want them, but we need to be realistic, and we need to go further. And we can do this in friendship and partnership between Belgium and India."
The latest agreements build on growing economic engagement between the two countries. A Belgian Economic Mission led by Princess Astrid in March 2025 brought together 338 participants from companies, chambers of commerce, academia and public institutions and resulted in 38 MoUs.De Wever also paid tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat on Thursday, where he laid a wreath and offered flowers before signing the visitor's book.The Belgian Prime Minister's visit is aimed at further strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation across trade, investment, defence, technology and connectivity, while also giving fresh momentum to India's engagement with the European Union and Europe.

Hanwha unveils drone-guided K9 howitzer concept in Estonia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
08:35:31 UTC
17:35:31 KST

- Hanwha unveiled a K9 howitzer concept using fire-guidance drones for target acquisition and battle damage assessment at Estonia's K9 User Club.
- The presentation follows Hanwha's $100.3 million US Army contract to build wheeled K9-based howitzer prototypes for the Mobile Tactical Cannon program.
Hanwha Aerospace showed off a new K9 howitzer operating concept built around fire-guidance drones this week, unveiling the plans at the fifth K9 User Club gathering in Estonia.
The three-day forum, hosted by the Estonian Defence Forces at the Estonian National Museum in Tartu from September 2 to 4, drew more than 200 military and industry representatives from seven K9 operator nations: South Korea, Estonia, Poland, Norway, Finland, Romania and Australia. Spain and Sweden sent observer delegations.
“The K9 has established itself as an outstanding and highly capable artillery system. Its performance, reliability, and operational capabilities have earned the trust of a growing number of NATO allies and partner nations,” said Major General Viktor Kalnitski, Deputy Commander of the Estonian Defence Forces.
“The K9 User Club brings together commanders, artillery officers, operators, technical specialists, and representatives of industry. It provides an opportunity to exchange practical experience and to discuss the challenges that each of us faces.”
The centerpiece of Hanwha’s presentation was an operating concept that pairs the K9 with a vertical take-off and landing drone for target acquisition and battle damage assessment. Hanwha said the drone detects and tracks targets, generates coordinates and transmits them to the K9’s fire-direction system, then stays over the target area to observe impacts and assess results after the engagement. The company said the approach is meant to shorten the time between spotting a target and firing on it, while reducing the need for forward observers in exposed positions.
Hanwha also presented wheeled artillery concepts that apply technology from the tracked K9A2, including its automated turret, to wheeled platforms. The company said the wheeled concepts are meant to offer greater mobility and deployment flexibility than the tracked K9 while drawing on the same underlying technology base.
The presentations follow a contract Hanwha Defense USA won from the US Army last month. On August 18, the Army awarded the company an Other Transaction Agreement worth $100.3 million initially, with a cumulative value of up to $262.9 million if all options are exercised, to build prototypes for the Army’s Mobile Tactical Cannon program. The deal covers six prototype wheeled self-propelled howitzers based on the K9 design, with an Army option for 12 more, and marks Hanwha Defense USA’s first major US Army contract. If the Army moves forward with fielding, the Mobile Tactical Cannon is intended to replace M777 towed howitzers in some formations.
Hanwha also used the Estonia forum to promote its TOMMS sustainment platform, a digital system for spare-parts procurement and logistics. The company said TOMMS combines requests for quotation, purchase orders and delivery tracking in one system and includes a catalog covering 700 to 800 frequently requested spare parts. Hanwha said it plans to link TOMMS to a spare-parts warehouse in Poland to support European K9 operators, and eventually use maintenance data to forecast parts demand before shortages occur.
“The K9 User Club has become much more than an annual gathering. It is a collaborative platform where users, operators and industry work together to transform operational experience into future capability development,” said Peter JK Bae, Senior Executive Vice President and Head of the MRO Business Division at Hanwha Aerospace. “Every lesson learned in the field helps shape the next generation of K9 capabilities, from new operating concepts and mobility solutions to smarter sustainment.”
More than 2,400 K9 family systems have been ordered by more than 10 countries across Europe, Africa and the Asia-Pacific region, according to Hanwha. The company’s roadmap for the platform includes the digitalized K9A1, the K9A2 with its automated turret, a future K9A3 designed for autonomous and uncrewed operation, and the wheeled artillery concepts shown this week.
Australia will host the next K9 User Club in 2027.

A West Bank resident was arrested on suspicion of involvement in the violent settler attacks on the Palestinian village of Kusra, the Israel Police announced on Thursday, marking the first suspect to be arrested in regard to the attacks.
According to the police, the 19-year-old suspect was arrested following a joint investigation with the Shin Bet (Israeli Security Agency) involving the collection of testimonies and evidence using "various technological tools and capabilities."
Police added that they aim to bring "everyone who took part" in the Kusra attacks to justice, noting that they plan to request an extension for the suspect's detention during his upcoming court hearing.
The Palestinian village has been the site of several recent violent attacks by extremist Israeli settlers, with the IDF responding by declaring the area a closed military zone.
Despite the designation, fifteen settlers entered the Palestinian village on August 15, though they did leave after the IDF arrived and explained the order to them, Army Radio reported at the time.
On Wednesday, an IDF commander was fired after he was filmed praying alongside Jewish extremists who had been involved in the Kusra attacks, with the commander's soldiers not punished for participating, as they believed they were following a lawful order.
The attacks have been described as a siege on the village, leading to an increased response by the IDF.
Settler leaders, Netanyahu condemn violent attacks in Kusra
Settler leaders have condemned the violence, saying on August 13 that the attacks in Kusra "are not our way."
The leaders, including the heads of the Yesha Council and Beit El Council, warned that the attacks were seriously damaging to Israel and the settlement movement.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also condemned the attacks, describing them on Saturday as "harming Israel's standing in the world."
His comments were followed by an interview with Channel 14's "The Patriots" broadcast on Sunday, during which Netanyahu claimed that the "small handful of young people" involved in the attacks face "all kinds of hardships from home."
Corinne Baum, Shir Perets, Reuters, Yonah Jeremy Bob, and Jerusalem Post Staff contributed to this report.

"As of today, the deployment of nuclear warheads beyond the places already hosting them is not on the [NATO] agenda," he told RMF FM.

Spain's PM Sanchez says no evidence Morocco orchestrated Ceuta border surge
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

08:31:56 UTC
17:31:56 KST

Spain has found no evidence to conclude that July's deadly border rush from Morocco into its enclave of Ceuta was orchestrated or carried out by Moroccan authorities, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told lawmakers on Thursday.
Sanchez's comments in the lower house of parliament followed a police report that emerged this week saying that the mass entry into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration event but a planned and phased operation designed to overwhelm border controls.
"I can assure you that no institution – not the diplomatic service, nor the European Commission, nor any international body – has provided the Spanish government with any solid evidence that Morocco planned or carried out the incident. None whatsoever," Sanchez said.
However, he said Morocco's Gendarmerie police allowed crossings during a key 10-hour period on July 30, when migrant arrivals peaked. Spanish authorities had yet to determine whether this was due to inaction or inability to contain the influx, Sanchez added.
Police report claims Moroccan security forces weakened, did not attempt to stop emigrants
The police report, seen by Reuters, alleged that Moroccan security forces were initially deployed in smaller numbers than usual near the Tarajal breakwater separating the enclave from the North African country and did not make a serious attempt to disperse the crowds.
Some uniformed Moroccan officers gave directions towards the crossing point, while other unidentified people appeared to guide or monitor the flow of people, the report said, but it did not identify individual officers or provide independently verified evidence of orders from Moroccan authorities.
Moroccan officials have denied enabling the crossing.

Sino Hero Ventures, a company registered in the British Virgin Islands, a reputed tax haven, initiated civil proceedings in the High Court on Wednesday accusing Koo and One Cool Film Production of failing to repay a HK$70 million loan the plaintiff extended on September 6, 2019.
Koo played a leading role in the 2024 blockbuster martial arts film, Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In, which has rekindled public interest in the Kowloon Walled City.
According to the writ, seen by the South China Morning Post on Thursday, the interest under the terms of the loan accrued at a monthly rate of 1 per cent, or 12 per cent per annum, and rose to 1.5 per cent per month, or 18 per cent per annually, in the event of a default in repayment.
The due date of repayment had been extended twice until the end of 2022, but the defendants had only repaid HK$13.9 million since January that year, the writ said.

Russia to close Goethe-Institut branches in response to German move

17:26:50 KST

Russia will close Goethe-Institut branches in Moscow, St. Petersburg and Yekaterinburg in response to Germany's decision to close the Russian House of Science and Culture in Berlin, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Thursday.
Speaking at a lecture organised by the Znanie Society on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, Lavrov rejected Russia's involvement in a drone incident at Leipzig Airport, Germany, in early August.
He said German authorities based their decision on an assumption that the drone resembled those used by Russia.
"There are Goethe-Institut branches in Moscow, St. Petersburg and Yekaterinburg. Of course, they will be closed after our cultural centre was expelled from there," Lavrov said.
"Otherwise, we would not respect ourselves," he added.
Lavrov said Germany's decision marked the end of its cultural presence in Russia, which had continued despite deteriorating relations over Ukraine.
The German government announced on September 1 that it would terminate the agreement governing the activities of the Russian House in Berlin following a drone incident at Leipzig Airport.
Germany attributed responsibility for the drone incident to Russia.
The Russian Embassy in Berlin rejected the accusation, describing the incident as a provocation and saying Germany's measures represented a serious escalation in bilateral relations.
Norwegian seizure of Russian vessel
Meanwhile, Norwegian authorities seized a Russian vessel in the Arctic archipelago of Svalbard on Wednesday at the request of Ukraine’s Naftogaz as part of a global effort to enforce a $4.22 billion arbitration award.
Naftogaz is trying to recover the multibillion-dollar arbitration award stemming from Russia’s 2014 illegal annexation of Crimea and its seizure of Ukrainian energy assets, including gas fields and pipelines.
In 2023, an arbitration tribunal in The Hague ordered Russia to pay the $4.22 billion to the Ukrainian state-owned energy company for unlawfully seizing its assets in Crimea.
After Russia's refusal to pay the award, Naftogaz has been petitioning national courts seeking court orders to seize Russian commercial assets.
“This is another important step towards restoring justice for Russia’s unlawful seizure of Naftogaz assets in Crimea. Russia cannot evade responsibility simply by refusing to comply with an international arbitral award. We will continue to pursue Russian assets around the world,” said Naftogaz CEO Sergii Fedorenko.
Norway’s seizure of the Russian vessel, the Professor Molchanov, comes after a Nord-Troms district court order issued on August 31, Svalbard Governor Lars Fause said in a statement.
Following the seizure, the vessel is not allowed to leave its current location in Barentsburg on Svalbard, the governor said.
The Russian vessel is used for commercial expedition cruises, including to Svalbard.

US locks on drone imports with up to 100pc tariffs
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
08:26:50 UTC
17:26:50 KST

New US tariffs of up to 100 percent took effect on Thursday on drones and certain components, as Washington pushes to lower its import reliance in an industry that China dominates.
US President Donald Trump signed an order setting out the duties in August, as the White House flagged "the national security threat posed by imports of drones and their components."
The order also aims to boost domestic supply chains.
Drones with a takeoff weight exceeding 25 kilogrammes, as well as those with thermal imaging capabilities and docking stations, face a 100 percent tariff.
Smaller drones face a 25 percent duty.
Some components of drones that are "not particularly sensitive" will also face duties, but those only come into effect on February 9.
China expressed opposition to the planned tariffs shortly after they were unveiled by Trump, with Beijing urging Washington to withdraw the duties.
A Commerce Ministry spokesman said the tariffs would "disrupt the global drone supply chain and further undermine a fair and competitive market environment."
He said China firmly opposed the move.
DJI, China's leading drone maker, which was founded in 2006, has captured more than two thirds of the global market in recent years, according to several studies.
Since 2022, however, DJI has been put on a list of companies determined to pose unacceptable risks to US national security.
DJI has fought its inclusion on the list. (AFP)

designboom guide to Paris Design Week 2026
Paris Design Week returns from September 10th to 19th, 2026, bringing exhibitions, installations, showrooms, galleries, and events to venues across the French capital. Taking place alongside Maison&Objet Pulse, the 2026 edition once again spreads across four districts, with designers and brands presenting new work in museums, historic buildings, galleries, boutiques, and public spaces.
With hundreds of events spread across the city, knowing where to begin can be a challenge. designboom’s guide to Paris Design Week 2026 highlights the exhibitions, installations, launches, and unexpected encounters worth seeking out, while designboom itself joins the program with paris.designboom, its temporary home at 72 rue des Archives, hosting podcast sessions, workshops, and the paris.designboom apéro, bringing together the wider design community for drinks and conversation.
illustration by Haus of Grace
MAISON&OBJET pulse 2026
Maison&Objet’s September edition returns as Maison&Objet Pulse, running from September 10th to 14th, 2026, at Paris Nord Villepinte. The new identity marks a shift for the fair, which positions its September edition around design in motion, emerging talent, craftsmanship, and new approaches to interior architecture, retail, and hospitality.
The theme for this edition, Pulse in Motion, focuses on movement, collective energy, and the role of design in bringing people together. Across seven sectors, the fair presents immersive spaces, new products, craftsmanship, materials, and emerging designers, alongside programs including Design District, Future On Stage, the Rising Talent Awards South Africa, and (im)Pulse.
For 2026, Valencia-based studio Masquespacio serves as ambassador for both Maison&Objet Pulse and Paris Design Week. The duo has developed installations for the fair and the city, as well as the visual identity for the September edition, bringing their colorful and expressive approach to the theme of movement.
where: Paris Nord Villepinte, ZAC Paris Nord 2, 93420 Villepinte, France
when: September 10th – 14th, 2026
visual by Studio Masquespacio
Paris Design Week Factory 2026
For its 2026 edition, Paris Design Week Factory brings together a new generation of designers across four venues in the Marais. Curated by Jean-Baptiste Durand and Simon Geringer, the program takes an intentionally open approach to emerging design, bringing together practices across design, art, and craftsmanship.
At Espace Commines, around 40 proposals are presented within a scenography conceived like a photographic studio, with each work isolated and framed to give it a sculptural presence. The exhibition continues at 116 rue de Turenne, where the works are arranged as a more experimental environment, allowing different objects and practices to overlap and enter into dialogue.

The pavilion’s reflective surfaces capture the surrounding trees, sky, and visitors, allowing the structure to visually shift with its environment. Yves de la Tour d’Auvergne — Plier la matière
Pulp Galerie presents Plier la matière, a retrospective of French designer and sculptor Yves de la Tour d’Auvergne (1927–2023), bringing together works from the 1980s and 1990s and focusing on the artist’s exploration of folding, a gesture he translated from paper into furniture and sculpture.
Initially trained as a painter, de la Tour d’Auvergne began experimenting with paper sculptures through an interest in light, using folding, tearing, and cutting to shape the material. He later developed a process combining resin and marble powder, allowing him to reproduce the whiteness and texture of paper while giving the works greater structural and sculptural qualities.
The exhibition includes the Alpha armchair (1982), Demi-Lune stool-table (1984), Olta chairs (1984), Albatros lamps (1988), Marmora chairs (1989), and Ellipse Pise table (1994). Across these pieces, the fold functions less as decoration than as a way of constructing form, organizing space, and catching light.

UK seeks vehicle-mounted laser defence against drone swarms
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
09:23:35 BST
17:23:35 KST

The Ministry of Defence has opened a competition for new counter-drone technologies intended to protect deployed troops from mass and low-cost aerial threats, with particular interest in laser directed-energy weapons and a requirement for an eventual system capable of autonomous operation from an Army vehicle, the UK Defence Journal understands.
The tender notice published on 2 September begins an iterative procurement process through the Commercial X Dynamic Market. The wider procurement carries an indicative value of £125 million excluding VAT, or £150 million including VAT, although the MOD makes clear that this funding has not yet been approved and later stages will depend on future funding decisions.
Setting out the operational requirement, the MOD stated: “Defence seeks additional capacity to detect, track, identify, decide and defeat mass and low-cost threats in a cost-effective manner and without being overwhelmed or exhausting stockpiles. This is particularly acute for deployed land forces, but the problem is applicable to the protection of defence fixed infrastructure in the homeland.”
On existing counter-UAS approaches, the notice states: “Current approaches are constrained by limited magazine depth, high cost-per-engagement, limited manoeuvrability, workforce intensity and the difficulty of adapting capabilities at pace as UAS threats evolve.” The MOD added: “Based on research, the Authority is particularly interested in capabilities centred on Laser Directed Energy Weapon (LDEW) effectors but is open to submissions relating to credible alternative novel approaches.”
The first phase will focus on technologies which already exist and could be accelerated towards a deployable system rather than procuring a finished counter-UAS capability immediately. The MOD stated: “The scope of Phase 1 is to identify and support organisations to accelerate development of their existing technology towards a final deployable system. It is not intended for the Phase 1 competition to seek delivery of a complete operational C-UAS system.”
For later phases, the department said: “Over later Phases, the Authority’s intent, aligned with their Integrated Procurement Model, is to identify and rapidly mature promising technologies as demonstrable Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). The Authority may then, at its discretion (and the criteria detailed below) select projects to be iteratively developed, integrated and proven as Minimum Deployable Capabilities (MDCs) for an initial operational user group.”
The notice continues: “Capabilities that demonstrate operational benefit may subsequently be developed further for wider adoption as part of a future Programme of Record. Suppliers will be notified of the criteria, selection processes, and competition format as these Phases arise.”
The intended configuration is also set out in the requirement. The MOD stated: “To address the challenge described above we are looking to deliver an integrated C-UAS force-protection capability capable of autonomous operation, mounted on an Army vehicle.”
On the attacks the system is expected to counter, the department said: “The capability should protect deployed troops against complex and saturation attacks designed to overwhelm existing defences or deplete conventional munition stocks. It should deliver more affordable combat mass against emerging air threats than legacy systems, and should exploit open architectures, platform-generated power, modular design and capable of autonomous operation.”
The initial threat focus is on representative Class 1 uncrewed aerial systems and related small aerial threats, covering single attacks as well as repeated, sequential and simultaneous profiles. The notice states that this includes threats intended to disrupt operations, conduct surveillance, target fixed or mobile assets, overwhelm local defences or force the disproportionate use of high-cost munitions.
The MOD also plans for the system to move beyond a crewed Army vehicle. It stated: “Integration of the capability onto a future uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV) is a planned objective. The solution should provide a scalable pathway towards future Army and Joint Ground-Based Air Defence (GBAD) capabilities as well as considering possible export opportunities.”
Stage 1 will assess whether industry proposals can meet the problem statements, with suppliers required to submit an evidence-based high-level programme plan supported by demonstrations, modelling, analysis and testing where appropriate. The MOD states: “No contract shall be awarded at this stage, but success is required to continue to Stage 2. All suppliers who demonstrate achievement of the threshold criteria shall be invited to Stage 2.”
Stage 2 will require successful suppliers to develop their initial proposals into fully costed and contractable projects running for around six months. Contracts at this point will be awarded according to evaluation scores and available funding within a £5 million limit, with technical factors expected to account for between 60% and 80% of the assessment and commercial factors between 20% and 40%.
Stage 3 could involve either a further competition or negotiation of a single direct award depending on how many suppliers remain. The MOD says contracts at that stage will cover scaling and production alongside testing, assurance, safety and security, with break points where aspects of the system cannot be demonstrated within the required timescales.
The department states: “The stated figure in this notice of £150,000,000 inc. VAT is aligned to the current understanding of the Strategic Defence Review, but this does not mean that this funding has been approved and is an indicative figure only.” It adds: “The intention is to begin Stage 1 with immediate effect, but future stages will not proceed until funding has been allocated and approved.”
The MOD also warns suppliers that later funding is not guaranteed, stating: “There is no guarantee that future funding will be allocated or approved and the Authority may cancel the procurement process at any time. Bidders proceed knowing and accepting this risk that no effort shall be compensated.”

Spain's PM Sanchez says no evidence Morocco orchestrated Ceuta border surge
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

17:21:15 KST

Spain's PM Sanchez says no evidence Morocco orchestrated Ceuta border surge
MADRID, Sept 3 - Spain has found no evidence to conclude that July's deadly border rush from Morocco into its enclave of Ceuta was orchestrated by Moroccan authorities, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Thursday, countering allegations in a Spanish police report.
Speaking in parliament, Sanchez responded to claims in the report that emerged this week suggesting the entry of over 70,000 people into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration but a planned effort to overwhelm border controls.
"I can assure you that no institution – not the diplomatic service, nor the European Commission, nor any international body – has provided the Spanish government with any solid evidence that Morocco planned or carried out the incident. None whatsoever," Sanchez said.
However, Moroccan police did allow crossings to occur during a key 10-hour period on July 30, when migrant arrivals peaked, he said. Spanish authorities had yet to determine whether this was due to inaction or inability to contain the influx, Sanchez added.
Sanchez has repeatedly defended Morocco during the crisis, highlighting Rabat's cooperation in returning the majority of the migrants in the days following the surge.
But on Thursday he said Spain summoned Morocco's ambassador on August 21 because of "unacceptable statements" made by two Moroccan ministers over Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's other North African enclave. Morocco's Justice Minister Abdellatif Ouahbi last month publicly reiterated Rabat's sovereignty claims over the cities.
FEWER MOROCCAN POLICE THAN USUAL AT BORDER
The police report, commissioned by a High Court judge last month and seen by Reuters, alleged that Moroccan security forces were initially deployed in smaller numbers than usual near the border breakwater and did not make a serious attempt to disperse the crowds.
Some uniformed Moroccan officers gave directions towards the crossing point, while other unidentified people appeared to guide or monitor the flow of people, the report said. It did not identify individual officers or provide independently verified evidence of orders from Moroccan authorities.
It cited some migrants as saying in interviews they had received guidance from Moroccan security forces to make the crossing.
"The police response in Morocco to the mobilisation and mass influx of migrants into Ceuta has been, to say the least, one of total permissiveness, with no serious attempt recorded to reduce, disperse or remove the crowd from the border perimeter," the report said.
Moroccan authorities did not respond to a Reuters request for comment but previously denied any permissiveness, blaming the crossing on traffickers, the misinterpretation of a Spanish court ruling that appeared to open a legal loophole for arrivals by sea and the use of social media to disseminate information about a mass crossing.
Justice Minister Ouahbi told Al Arabiya TV on August 22 that Moroccan authorities did not attempt to stop people marching toward Ceuta in order to avoid bloodshed, but they handled the crisis "wisely and with sang-froid".
The police report said trafficking groups in Morocco could mobilise a maximum of about 300 migrants a day, lacking the capacity to orchestrate an event of those dimensions. REUTERS
