US declares it will accelerate military presence in Australia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:59:13 UTC
13:59:13 KST

US declares it will accelerate military presence in Australia
In short:
Defence Minister Richard Marles met with his US counterpart, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, in Washington DC and discussed US "force posture" in Australia.
Any expansion would come on top of the existing US presence in Australia, including US Marine rotations through Darwin and the creation of Submarine Rotational Force—West in WA.
What's next?
Mr Marles also met with AI companies and flagged announcements about an expanded US military presence are expected in coming months.
The US military's presence in Australia is set to grow further, with the defence minister flagging upcoming announcements on a greater US "force posture" on Australian soil.
Richard Marles met with his US counterpart, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, in Washington DC and discussed an expansion of the US presence on Australian military bases.
The United States already has a significant military presence in Australia through existing force posture agreements, including the annual rotation of US Marines through Darwin, and the establishment of Submarine Rotational Force — West at HMAS Stirling near Perth.
About 1,000 US Navy personnel are set to be based at HMAS Stirling from next year to support American Virginia-class submarines operating out of the naval base.
Mr Marles said the US military presence will grow further, with announcements expected when he and Foreign Minister Penny Wong meet their US counterparts in the next few months.
"You'll hear more from us about what [those changes] are at AUSMIN when we meet," he said.
"But ... since we've come to government, you can see a through-line of growing American force in Australia, and we think that's really important in terms of providing deterrence in the Indo-Pacific, providing for stability and peace in the Indo-Pacific.
"And that's very much in Australia's national interest."
The Pentagon's readout of the meeting pointed to plans to grow the American military presence in Australia by "accelerat[ing] force posture initiatives at Australian bases".
It suggested greater military-industrial cooperation between the two countries, including guided missile production.
Australia signed a "force posture agreement" with Washington in 2014 aimed at securing the presence of US forces in Australia over the long term on the grounds it helps provide stability within the region, and assists with a quick response to humanitarian disasters.
The readout also pointed to the sensitive issue of defence spending, as the US continues to pressure allies to substantially lift investment in their militaries.
"Secretary Hegseth emphasized the need for capable allies to contribute to the collective defense and invest in their own sovereign security," it said.
Asked about Australia's defence spending, Mr Marles said recent spending increases have been "well received".
"We now have defence spending at 2.8 per cent of GDP by the NATO measure, which puts us ahead of most NATO countries, with the exception of the Nordics, the Baltics, Poland, that kind of front line," he said.
"That means our spending on this day, in respect of defence, is ahead of Germany, ahead of Britain, ahead of France, ahead of Spain, ahead of Italy.
"All of that is understood. We have one of the highest spends on defence in the Indo-Pacific."
Confidence on AUKUS
The defence minister also reiterated his confidence that Australia will be delivered its first Virginia-class submarine as planned.
Under the AUKUS agreement, Australia will buy three second-hand Virginia-class submarines from the US in the 2030s, with the first to be delivered in 2032.
But the then-US president will have the final sign-off on whether the sale goes ahead, considering the US's own needs at the time.
Mr Marles was asked about his confidence that a future US administration will honour the deal, and argued other elements of AUKUS, like Australia's investment in submarine maintenance facilities in Western Australia. He said this is an important offering for the US that can keep its submarines active in critical parts of the world for longer.
"The establishment of Submarine Rotation Force — West, as well as the establishment of the Henderson Defence Precinct, offers the opportunity for US Navy submarines to undergo maintenance much closer to their critical area of operation, which creates sea days for the United States Navy," he said.
"And that's ultimately why this is such an important agreement from the United States point of view. That's why they're walking down this path."
AI links
Earlier this week Mr Marles met with a number of the world's leading tech companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft and Google while visiting San Francisco.
The federal government has been pushing to build stronger links with top AI companies in the hope of attracting US investment into Australian-based data centres.
Treasury estimates suggest the construction of data centres in Australia to be worth about $150 billion by 2030.
But the government has flagged its desire to see more than just a financial return for hosting data centres, including guaranteed and affordable access to computing power for Australian businesses.
Mr Marles said securing more investment into AI in Australia is both an economic and national security priority, but there are also sensitive questions around community support.
"The whole point of what we've done in terms of articulating AI standards is to make sure that we are doing this in the right way in Australia, that we get the planning right so that the data centres are placed in appropriate places," he said.
"That they come with power, so that the power infrastructure that is created to power these data centres actually makes a contribution to our overall power grid rather than taking from it.
"In terms of the investment that these companies are looking at making, to be honest that's a welcome message from their perspective. Without a social license this doesn't get done."
He argues building relationships with companies developing frontier AI models is also critical for the Australian Defence Force, given the role AI is expected to play on future battlefields.
"When we look at all of the major platforms that we are operating today, going forward AI will have a part in respect of them," he said.
"And that's why this is such an important sovereignty question; it really matters that we have access to this technology."

France's world-first fast fashion laws take hit Shein and Temu with new fees
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:52:41 UTC
13:52:41 KST

Items from "ultra-fast fashion" brands like Temu and Shein are subject to new fees under France's world-first efforts to curb the overconsumption of cheap clothing.
The fees are part of a law imposed in June which aimed to address environmental concerns from overproduction of garments and its impact on the environment.
They are the toughest laws a country has imposed on fast fashion e-commerce brands responsible for manufacturing and selling millions of garments each year.
French shoppers spent $3.2 billion on textile products in 2025, an average of 43 items per person, according to French eco-organisation ReFashion.
In comparison, the Australia Institute estimates Australians purchased about 56 items per person over the same period.
But there are no such penalties for wastage by fast fashion brands or a governing body for the disposal of garments in Australia.
So why is France so strict and what do the laws entail?
What are the laws?
The main aim of the fast fashion legislation is to address surging sales of cheap clothing sold by brands like Shein, Temu and AliExpress.
But it also bans "ultra-fast fashion" advertising in France, including on social media and through paid partnerships with influencers.
"These platforms are false champions of consumer purchasing power," Commerce Minister Serge Papin told local newspaper Ouest France.
"They sell at low prices, yet their products often fail to meet standards and lack durability."
Neither Shein nor Temu responded to Reuters' requests for comment on the fees.
How do they work?
The French fees are calculated using a formula that takes into account the number of products available under a brand, their prices and how easily they can be repaired.
It makes France the first EU member to penalise retailers based on the number of items they offer on their website.
Shein, for example, had a product selection of more than 2 million items as of March 31 this year, with 4,700 new apparel items each day.
The new fees range from €0.25 (24 AUD cents) for a pair of boxer shorts or socks to €12 ($22.57) for a coat, with the amount capped at 50 per cent of the product's pre-tax sales price.
They will be higher by 2030.
What about other European laws?
The European Union has implemented other measures to crack down on the environmental impact of fast fashion in the past five years.
In July, the EU began prohibiting large companies from destroying unsold clothing, known as the "eco-design for sustainable products" regulation.
Previously, in September 2025, the European Parliament introduced a set of rules that guide how member states should establish schemes that recover the cost of collecting, sorting and recycling excess products and wastage from garment and textile producers.
The laws were a response to an EU report that found textile consumption had climbed to an average of 19 kilograms per person in 2022.
About the same time, "extended producers' responsibility" (EPR) schemes were being set up in individual EU member states, including France, Sweden and the Netherlands.
The Dutch EPR body, Stitching UPV Textiel, will collect fees from retailers based on the volume of clothing they sell in the Netherlands, not the size of their range.
What has the response been like?
The fees came into effect after Shein, which was founded in China and is headquartered in Singapore, was valued at US$26.2 billion on its first day of public trading on the Hong Kong stock market this week.
The company was once estimated to be worth up to $100 billion, but the value appears to have fallen due to competition, trade restrictions and questions of its ethics.
Shein and Temu have not recently responded publicly to the implementation of the laws.
Shein's spokesperson in France, Quentin Ruffat, has previously said the fast fashion charges would hurt customers by pushing prices up.
European fast fashion brands like H&M and Zara are not expected to be impacted by the new laws due to the smaller range of items they carry.
This has drawn criticism from the French Green party and environmental groups.
What about Australia?
Australia is the highest consumer of textiles per person in the world, according to Clean Up Australia.
More than 200,000 tonnes of clothing ends up in Australian landfill each year.
Australia has no legal restrictions on the sale of fast fashion and the wastage of fast fashion.
Instead, it relies on a voluntary national stewardship scheme called Seamless.
Funded in part by an Australian government grant, Seamless aims to deliver a program to "support a coordinated national clothing collection, sorting, reuse and recycling system for Australia".
The scheme is funded by a 4 cent garment levy paid by signatories to the scheme.
Only eight out of 30 Australian fashion brands signed on to the scheme: Big W, David Jones, The Iconic, RM Williams, Rip Curl, Lorna Jane, The Sussan Group and Cotton On.
ABC/Wires

ICAO updates recommendations on protecting civil aviation in conflict zones
This is said in a statement published on the organization’s website, according to Ukrinform.
“ICAO is observing heightened risks of civil aircraft being targeted or caught in crossfire, and while the aviation industry is able to reroute flights and maintain operations during conflicts, this operational flexibility does not address the fundamental security threat,” the statement says.
According to the statement, threats to civil aviation have increased significantly due to the use of advanced military technologies, including long-range weapons, unmanned aerial vehicles, advanced air defense systems, and means of jamming radio frequencies used by global navigation satellite systems.
“ICAO is updating its Manual Concerning Safety Measures relating to Military Activities and its Risk Assessment Manual for Civil Aircraft Operations Over or Near Conflict Zones, which focus on how authorities and airlines and air navigation services providers can better assess threats from malicious activities,” the statement says.
The UN specialized agency reminded its member states that they must rapidly share information on threats to civil aircraft, strengthen risk-assessment and decision-making mechanisms, and improve coordination between military and civilian authorities to prevent civilian aircraft from being mistakenly identified as military targets.
“The International Civil Aviation Organization is reiterating its calls for stronger commitments from all Member States to protect civilian aircraft from all risks arising from conflict zones,” the organization stressed.
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukraine officially informed ICAO that Russian airspace is dangerous for civil aviation due to increased military activity and called on all parties to avoid it.

New US tariffs on drones take effect
- The US has imposed tariffs up to 100% on drones and parts to reduce reliance on Chinese imports and protect national security.
- Drones over 25kg and those with thermal imaging face the highest tariffs, while smaller drones have a 25% duty.
- China opposes the tariffs, warning they disrupt global supply chains, with DJI, a major Chinese drone maker, affected by US restrictions since 2022.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – New US tariffs of up to 100 per cent took effect on Sept 3 on drones and certain components, as Washington pushes to lower its import reliance in an industry that China dominates.
US President Donald Trump signed an order setting out the duties in August, as the White House flagged “the national security threat posed by imports of drones and their components”. The order also aims to boost domestic supply chains.
Drones with a take-off weight exceeding 25kg, as well as those with thermal imaging capabilities and docking stations, face a 100 per cent tariff.
Smaller drones face a 25 per cent duty.
Some components of drones that are “not particularly sensitive” will also face duties, but those come into effect only on Feb 9, 2027.
China expressed opposition to the planned tariffs shortly after they were unveiled by Trump, with Beijing urging Washington to withdraw the duties.
A commerce ministry spokesman said the tariffs would “disrupt the global drone supply chain and further undermine a fair and competitive market environment”.
He said China firmly opposed the move.
Chinese company DJI, which was founded in 2006, has captured more than two-thirds of the global drone market in recent years, according to several studies.
Since 2022, however, DJI has been on a US list of Chinese firms linked to the country’s military and subject to restrictions on access to US technology. DJI has fought its inclusion on the list. AFP

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taipei prosecutors have indicted 57 people over an alleged romance scam that used AI voice-changing technology and fake dating profiles to defraud more than 20,000 people of at least NT$900 million (US$28.3 million), per PTS.
Prosecutors on Wednesday concluded their investigation and indicted Huang Chien-hao (黃建豪), his wife Hsu Hsiang-chi (許湘琦), and 55 others on charges including fraud and money laundering. Prosecutors are seeking a prison sentence of 25 years for Huang and 18 years for Hsu, who allegedly played leading roles in the operation.
According to investigators, the group began in 2022, recruiting members to create fake female profiles on dating platforms with photographs of attractive women. After potential victims were contacted, members allegedly developed relationships with them and encouraged them to purchase expensive products or send gifts.
To make the fake relationships appear authentic, the group allegedly used AI voice-changing software that allowed male employees and older women to sound like young women. Chiang Chia-sheng (江嘉勝), deputy commander of the Criminal Investigation Bureau's 4th Investigation Corps, said the group also assigned female escorts to meet victims in person to strengthen their confidence in the purported relationships, per PTS.
Prosecutors said the group also developed an iAssistant system to track employee performance, with those failing to meet performance targets allegedly subjected to severe physical and sexual punishments. Authorities have launched a separate investigation into this matter.
Prosecutors said the alleged scam left some victims deeply in debt after they exhausted their savings or borrowed money to meet the group's demands.
The case has also raised concerns about the increasing sophistication of AI voice-cloning technology. National Chung Hsing University Computer Science Professor Fan Yao-chung (范耀中) said current voice-changing technology can make it difficult to determine a person's identity based solely on their voice, per LTN.
Fan said one way to test a suspicious caller is to interrupt them while they are speaking, as current systems can sometimes have difficulty responding naturally when unexpectedly interrupted. Speaking Taiwanese or other languages can also pose challenges for some AI systems, he said. However, Fan warned such techniques may become less effective as the technology improves.
He also recommended asking questions that only the purported caller should know and verifying information through multiple independent sources rather than relying on a person's voice to confirm their identity.
The case has also prompted discussion about why romance scams continue to succeed despite years of public warnings. Author Ellen Huang (黃越綏) said romance scams are not a new phenomenon, noting that earlier versions included scams involving pen pals and handwritten letters. What has changed, she said, is the ability of organized groups to exploit personal information and technology on a much larger scale.

Less urgent projects will be postponed or reconsidered, while obsolete equipment will be phased out.

New Taipei clinic shut after 11 contract hepatitis C
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:39:13 UTC
13:39:13 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — A clinic in New Taipei's Banqiao District has been ordered to suspend operations and fined NT$300,000 (US$9,439) after 11 patients who received nutritional injections there were diagnosed with acute hepatitis C.
The Centers for Disease Control said Wednesday that nine of the 11 patients had hepatitis C virus sequences showing 99.7% to 100% similarity, strongly suggesting that the infections share a common source.
The CDC and New Taipei Department of Health have identified 1,118 people who received injections at Antai Songhe Clinic (安泰淞鶴診所) since July 1, 2025, and are expanding the investigation to determine whether additional infections occurred, per SETN.
The investigation began after health authorities received a report on Aug. 12 that two members of the same Banqiao family had developed acute hepatitis C. An epidemiological investigation found that both had received nutritional injections at the clinic.
A third family member who had also received injections at the clinic was subsequently diagnosed with acute hepatitis C, prompting authorities to broaden the investigation. The CDC and New Taipei health officials conducted an unannounced inspection of the clinic on Aug. 20 and returned on Aug. 26 with infection-control experts.
Officials found multiple violations involving injection and hygiene practices, including improper sterilization, failure to disinfect surfaces, and failure to wash hands before and after patient contact. Investigators also found needles left inserted into the rubber stoppers of medication vials, allowing them to be used repeatedly to draw medication.
Prefilled syringes were found in both the medical preparation area and other areas of the clinic, and no appropriate containers were found for disposing of sharp objects. Medications, blood samples, and personal items were also stored together in the same refrigerator, according to the CDC.
CDC Director-General Lo Yi-chun (羅一鈞) said the preliminary assessment indicates that the cluster likely originated from a common source and was not caused by direct transmission from medical personnel to patients, per LTN.
Authorities believe inadequate infection control and safe injection procedures may have allowed the hepatitis C virus to contaminate needles, medication vials, or the surrounding environment, resulting in cross-infection among patients.
New Taipei authorities ordered the clinic to suspend all operations on Tuesday until it passes a follow-up inspection. The physician responsible for the clinic has also been referred for disciplinary action, with the maximum possible penalty being revocation of their medical license.
Clinic manager and physician Sun Hao-yang (孫浩陽) acknowledged shortcomings in the facility's infection-control procedures but denied that staff had used the same needle on different patients. Sun also disputed a direct connection between the hepatitis C infections and medical procedures performed at the clinic, according to SETN.
CDC officials warned that additional cases could emerge as the expanded screening proceeds. Authorities estimate that between 5% and 10% of the 1,118 people could eventually test positive for hepatitis C, per UP Media.
Hepatitis C is a bloodborne infection that can cause chronic liver disease, cirrhosis, and liver cancer if left untreated. The CDC said oral antiviral medications for acute and chronic hepatitis C are covered by Taiwan's National Health Insurance system and have high cure rates.

“Like many people in Makati, I left home in search of better opportunities. One day, I jokingly referred to myself as an ‘OFW in Makati’ and it resonated,” Tumbagahan said.

"As you heard, the president noted yesterday that the terms of the grain deal discussed with Western partners were not fulfilled. This includes issues related to reconnecting Rosselkhozbank to SWIFT. These factors, including restrictions on processing payments for food, will have long-term consequences for the global food system," Listov said.

Listov noted that these figures could clearly have been significantly higher without sanctions restrictions and unresolved issues under the grain deal.
"Despite this, Russian farmers continue to meet their obligations to international partners, while Rosselkhozbank provides comprehensive support to export-oriented companies. Since the beginning of the year, we have allocated 541 bln rubles to finance agricultural exports, up 14.2% from last year," he concluded.
Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier said at the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan that the measures promised by the West under the grain deal, including lifting sanctions on Rosselkhozbank and removing restrictions on ships entering ports, had never been implemented.

The City of Copenhagen is ready to send more displaced Ukrainians to Jutland after five Jutland mayors opposed the government’s bill to halt immigration from 14 Ukrainian regions in Jyllands-Posten.
Andreas Keil, Social Democrats, Mayor of Employment, Integration, and Business, wrote this in a letter to the mayors.
“If you have the opportunity to receive a number of displaced Ukrainians, it will be a great help to Copenhagen,” he wrote in the letter.
He further writes that it will simultaneously be a concrete contribution to the redistribution among municipalities that Minister for Immigration and Integration Morten Bødskov (Social Democrats as well) has previously requested.
“I understand it to mean that the five Jutland municipalities would like more settlement, labor, and have more opportunities to accommodate the newcomers, while we, conversely, in Copenhagen are challenged to find accommodation for more than the 3,800 Ukrainians we already accommodate now,” he stated.
The letter has been sent to the mayors of Hjørring, Lemvig, Vesthimmerland, Skive, and Brønderslev Municipality, respectively.

====================================================================================================

Global resonance of Xi's selfless commitment to the people
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
12:13:49 CST
13:13:49 KST

Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 31, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
On the morning of August 31, during talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov expressed admiration for the remarkable development achievements China has made under the leadership of Xi, and voiced willingness to learn from China's experience in state governance, particularly Xi's commitment to the people, as embodied in his words, "I will fully commit to the people and never fail them."
In March 2019, during his state visit to Italy, Xi met with Roberto Fico, then president of the Italian Chamber of Deputies.
Fico asked Xi, "What did you feel when you were elected Chinese president?"
"Governing such a huge country requires a strong sense of responsibility and hard work," said Xi. "For the good of my people, I will put aside my own well-being. I am willing to be selfless and devote myself to China's development."
Xi has spoken of this conviction on multiple occasions. During his trip to the United States in November, 2023, Xi recalled in a speech at a welcome dinner hosted by friendly organizations that, before turning 16, he was in a village in northern Shaanxi Province, where he lived and farmed with villagers, and knew about their worries and needs. He said that, over the past half-century, he had always felt confident and strong when staying with the people. “Serving the people selflessly and living up to their expectations is my lifelong commitment,” he said.
Xi not only keeps in mind major issues concerning the national economy and people's livelihood, but also cares about the everyday concerns of ordinary people.
During his local inspection tours, Xi chatted with local residents about their daily lives and household finances, felt the quilts on their beds to make sure they stay warm, lifted the lids of cooking pots to see whether they eat well, asked about whether they had rich cultural and spiritual lives, and attached great importance to the healthy development of young people.
From securing a decisive victory in poverty alleviation to comprehensively advancing rural revitalization, from achieving a moderately prosperous society in all respects to marching toward common prosperity, Chinese Communists in the new era have borne in mind the country's most fundamental interests — ensuring that the people live happy lives. They have devoted themselves wholeheartedly to this cause, forged ahead undauntedly to achieve it, and made persistent efforts to bring it to fruition.
People's well-being is of utmost importance in Chinese modernization. China's development achievements vividly demonstrate its people-centered development philosophy. China now has the world's largest education, social security and healthcare systems, while achieving historic strides in making education universally available. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, average life expectancy in China rose to 79.25 years, more than 12 million new urban jobs were created each year on average, and direct settlement of cross-provincial medical expenses benefited 560 million medical visits nationwide.
In the opening year of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, China's head-of-state diplomacy has witnessed one highlight after another, with more and more foreign leaders seeking inspiration from China's governance model for their own development.
During his state visit to China, Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo made a special trip to Banyan Village of Huzhu Tu Autonomous County in northwest China's Qinghai Province, where Xi Jinping visited during an inspection tour in 2016. "Seeing is believing. With China's targeted poverty alleviation policies effectively implemented, Banyan Village has undergone tremendous changes, which is truly inspiring." Chapo said, adding that the experience is also exemplary for the world.
At the entrance of Yucun Village in Anji County, east China’s Zhejiang Province, Thongloun Sisoulith, General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party Central Committee and Lao President, took a photo of the inscription carved on a boulder, which reads, "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets." After hearing a briefing on the "Green Rural Revival Program" — which was initiated in June 2003 by Xi, then secretary of the CPC Zhejiang Provincial Committee, with a plan to renovate about 10,000 incorporated villages in five years and transform about 1,000 central villages among them into examples of moderate prosperity in all respects — Thongloun lauded the program as remarkable for creating countless beautiful villages.
During Xi’s visit to Kyrgyzstan, how to further improve people's well-being remains a key concern for him. "Pursuing high-quality cooperation on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, a transportation artery carrying the region's aspirations for development," "further promoting personnel exchanges and strengthening cooperation in such areas as youth, media, tourism, sports, and medical care, and at subnational levels," and "steadily consolidating the societal foundation of and popular support for China-Kyrgyzstan friendship" — these are among the priorities highlighted by Xi.
"The people's aspiration for a better life is what we are striving for." This deep commitment to the people is reflected in practice, offers inspiration for the future, and allows the international community to gain a deeper appreciation of the CPC's people-centered governance philosophy and its strong sense of mission and responsibility.
"I will fully commit to the people and never fail them." This is not merely a powerful pledge, but a commitment translated into concrete action. The vision of enabling hundreds of millions of people to live better lives is resonating more widely around the world.

Feature: Malaysian artists interpret Nanyang Chinese culture through dance
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
12:13:35 CST
13:13:35 KST

KUALA LUMPUR, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- At Dewan Filharmonik PETRONAS (DFP), Malaysia's first dedicated classical concert venue in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, dancers from different ethnic backgrounds are rehearsing Chinese dance. As the music begins, they stretch, leap and turn, blending the grace and fluidity of Chinese dance with the movement vocabulary of contemporary dance.
Malaysia's ASK Dance Company and Dua Space Dance Theatre will jointly present a performance themed A Dance Spectacular, scheduled for Sept. 5 at the concert hall. The two local dance companies will bring their own interpretations of Chinese dance to audiences by combining traditional and contemporary elements.
Joseph Gonzales, founder of ASK Dance Company, said he was both surprised and excited when the company was invited to create a performance centered on Chinese dance. Although ASK is better known for its contemporary works, many of its dancers have received training in Chinese dance.
Gonzales said the cast includes Malay and Chinese dancers, as well as dancers of other ethnic backgrounds. For him, performers from different cultural backgrounds interpreting Chinese dance through their own bodies reflects the unique character of Malaysia's multicultural society.
In ASK Dance Company's Pearl of the Orient, a piece inspired by Mongolian dance brings the imagery of vast grasslands of northern China onto the stage. Contemporary elements are incorporated into traditional movements.
Gonzales said the choreography is not simply intended to demonstrate technique but also to allow audiences to experience the cultural meanings embodied in the movements.
As Pearl of the Orient unfolds, its narrative journey moves from China to Nanyang, or Southeast Asia. With migration as a central thread, the work uses scenes and imagery including sword dance, tin miners, romance, mahjong and Chinese New Year celebrations to tell the story of Chinese migrants who came to Malaysia and gradually developed a distinctive local cultural identity.
For Anthony Meh Kim Chuan, co-founder of Dua Space Dance Theatre, learning Chinese dance is likewise not about simply reproducing a dance form from China.
Living and working in a multicultural environment, he said, means that different artistic traditions naturally become part of the dancers' physical vocabulary, gradually shaping a distinctly Malaysian form of expression. Meh hopes these diverse cultural experiences will eventually develop into a Chinese dance expression with Malaysian characteristics.
That exploration is also reflected in the performance Passage Into The Unknown: Earth, Water, Fire, Wind. Drawing inspiration from the four elements, the work uses dance to explore the fluidity and transformation of water, the nurturing qualities of earth, the relationship between fire and civilization, and wind as a symbol of cycles and continuity.
While drawing on Chinese cultural and philosophical ideas, the work also connects them with Malaysia's multicultural experience. For Meh, the process is also an attempt to give Chinese cultural imagery new expression on the Malaysian stage.
A younger generation of Malaysian dancers is also joining this exploration, including several performers trained in Chinese dance, some of whom have pursued further studies at the Beijing Dance Academy.
Gonzales said he hopes to bring together dance experiences from China and Malaysian arts institutions, providing more opportunities for young artists to create and present Chinese dance.
From traditional Chinese dance movements to Malaysian music and everyday cultural experiences, and from ethnic Chinese performers to dancers of diverse backgrounds sharing the same stage, Chinese dance is taking on new forms through interpretation and re-creation by Malaysian artists.
"Dance really represents culture," Gonzales said, adding that in a multicultural society like Malaysia, people need not only to understand one another's cultures, but also to appreciate them. ■

Factbox: Latest relief and rescue progress at mudslide-hit border port in China's Xizang
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
12:13:32 CST
13:13:32 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, causing heavy casualties and leaving many missing.
Chinese rescuers immediately launched all-out search and rescue operations. Here is what we know about the deadly mudslide and the latest progress in China:
-- Twenty-one people have been confirmed dead and 541 others remain missing after the mudslide struck the border port, according to the regional government's latest news briefing.
-- An ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-mountain glacier in Nepal has been identified as the cause of the mudslide.
-- Rescuers have recovered 847 pieces of personal belongings, according to the news briefing. Local authorities have received 876 phone calls from the relatives of the victims and missing people, and have been promptly replying to their requests.
-- To date, some 2,300 rescue personnel, more than 400 search and rescue vehicles, over 8,000 sets of professional equipment, over 800 drone flights and 24 helicopter flights have been deployed. A total of 5.43 tonnes of materials and equipment have been airdropped to the area.
-- Telecom operators have restored 12 base stations in the port area, ensuring communications for emergency command, rescue operations and supply coordination.
-- At the core affected zone, some 336 rescuers have conducted multiple rounds of thorough and exhaustive search and rescue operations, covering a cumulative area of 1.591 million square meters.
-- Road access to the zone was basically restored at 10 a.m. Wednesday after days of round-the-clock repair work on the G216. Over 10 pieces of heavy machinery have entered the core area to aid on-site rescuers.
-- China will continue to share information on barrier lake risks, glacial lake risks and emergency hydrological monitoring with Nepal to support disaster rescue and relief efforts, an official with the Ministry of Water Resources said Wednesday.
The ministry is now providing Nepal with daily updates on the development of a barrier lake above Gyirong Port, cascading risks associated with the Cuojian River impact crater in Nepal, glacial lake risks in the Gyirong Zangbo River basin, the development and risk forecasts of new barrier lakes, and emergency hydrological monitoring.
The geological conditions in Gyirong disaster-hit area remain highly unstable, with risks of further landslides, rockfalls and other secondary hazards, the ministry warned. The large number of glacial lakes in the surrounding area is also adding to the uncertainty.
-- China's meteorological authorities have been providing Nepal with weather monitoring, forecasting, early warning and impact services after the mudslide, said Wang Yawei, a spokesperson for the China Meteorological Administration, on Wednesday.
Wang said at a press conference that the administration held video weather consultations with Nepal's meteorological department immediately after the disaster, and has actively provided meteorological support for Nepal's rescue and relief operations.
-- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told a regular press briefing that China is preparing a third batch of emergency relief supplies, including Bailey bridges, epidemic prevention materials and emergency communications equipment. China is ready to send a second group of DNA identification experts based on Nepal's needs, he added. ■

"I made thorough preparations for this match. I controlled the rhythm well throughout, played solid, and stayed highly focused. It hasn't been easy for me, my recent form wasn't great, and I came to this US Open without a technical coach, fitness trainer, or physiotherapist," Wu said.
In the women's singles second round, Wang Xinyu failed to advance after losing 7-5, 2-6, 6-3 to 21st seed Anna Kalinskaya.
"It was a pity to lose the first set because I hesitated on my attack. I played really well in the second set, but my opponent raised her level in the decider, which was a good learning experience for me," Wang said.
"I gained a lot from several matches during the North American swing, which will help me play more decisively. I want to stay committed to my own style. I still have the doubles ahead, and I'm grateful for everyone's support," she added. ■

Duplantis embraces Ultimate innovation, looks ahead to 2027 Beijing worlds
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
12:13:28 CST
13:13:28 KST

BUDAPEST, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- Pole vault world record holder Armand Duplantis said Wednesday that athletics needs to embrace innovation ahead of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship, while he and several other top athletes also expressed excitement about the 2027 World Athletics Championships in Beijing.
"I think it was about time to try something and innovate a bit within athletics," the 26-year-old Swede said during an online media session.
The inaugural Ultimate Championship will be held in Budapest from September 11 to 13. Duplantis said the new event gives elite athletes a major target in years without an Olympic Games or World Championships.
"You want to have some sort of climax, and you want to build something towards the year," he said.
Duplantis welcomed the competition's new approach and the chance to bring the world's best athletes together on one stage.
"When you have all the best there and the stage is set, then we're athletes and we're going to show up to the moment and perform when we need to," Duplantis said.
The Swede also stressed the importance of attracting more spectators to athletics, saying prize money matters but the sport's long-term future depends on drawing a larger audience.
"We want eyeballs and we want people to watch," he said. "At the end of the day, it is entertainment, and we have to be the most entertaining that we possibly can be."
American sprinter Melissa Jefferson-Wooden said the Ultimate Championship will give athletes a "new feel," contrasting its compact format with the traditional World Championships, where athletes must navigate several rounds over a longer schedule.
Olympic long jump champion Tara Davis-Woodhall made a similar point, saying the Ultimate Championship emphasizes producing one's best performance on the day, while the World Championships test endurance through qualifying rounds and finals.
"They're both different experiences. They're both different mind challenges," she said.
For Duplantis, Budapest is also a place where he hopes to push the limits again. The Swede said he loves the National Athletics Center and believes the venue has "world record capacity."
"That's my goal, and that's what I want to achieve for sure," he said.
Looking ahead to Beijing 2027, several athletes expressed excitement about competing in China's capital.
Jefferson-Wooden said it will be her first trip to China and that she is keen to experience a new championship atmosphere.
Davis-Woodhall highlighted the appeal of a multiday World Championships, including the chance to watch other events and spend time with teammates.
Botswanan sprinter Letsile Tebogo, who won gold in the 200m at the 2024 Olympics, said he had good memories of competing at Diamond League meetings in China and looked forward to returning next year.
Duplantis, who has competed in several Chinese cities, described Beijing as a "bucket-list place" and the Bird's Nest as a stadium with "a lot of power" and an energy an athlete could "only dream of."
"I'm really excited for it because I know that the Chinese fans can really show up and show out," Duplantis said. "So I think it's going to be great." ■

VLADIVOSTOK, September 3. /TASS/. The Russian economy is in a state of "overcooling," and it is time to shift toward policies aimed at supporting and stimulating investment growth, Sberbank CEO Herman Gref told reporters on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum (EEF).
"Yes, that's what we believe. As of today, I think it's already obvious. There is always some wordplay involved here. The question is what meaning we attach to these terms. The Central Bank speaks of a gradual slowdown, while we call the situation cooling, or already overcooling. As of today, the figures speak for themselves," he said in response to a question.
Gref noted that all these factors indicate that it is time to shift toward policies aimed at supporting and stimulating investment growth. "Businesses need help," he stressed.
Sberbank also intends to provide all possible assistance to marketplaces and sellers affected by drone attacks, Gref added.
The Eastern Economic Forum is being held on September 1-4 in Vladivostok on the campus of Far Eastern Federal University. The forum is organized by the Roscongress Foundation with the support of the Russian government. TASS is the general information partner.

VLADIVOSTOK, September 3. /TASS/. Russia has recorded no decline in trade with Iran amid developments in and around the Islamic Republic thanks to the free trade agreement between the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and Iran, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexey Overchuk said at the Eastern Economic Forum (EEF).
"One of our major achievements was the agreement with Iran coming into force last year. We are also extending the North-South [corridor] there. Despite what is happening in and around Iran today, this agreement allows us to maintain trade volumes. In other words, against the backdrop of everything that is happening, we are seeing no decline in trade volumes," he said.

Pesticides poison nearly half of world’s farmers each year – study
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:10:58 UTC
13:10:58 KST

Pesticides poison nearly half of world’s farmers each year – study
Nearly half of the world’s estimated 934 million farmers suffer unintentional pesticide poisoning each year, according to a study published Wednesday in the journal Frontiers in Public Health.
The study, conducted by researchers from the Pesticide Action Network (PAN), analyzed 214 publications from 2006 to 2023 alongside World Health Organization mortality data. It estimated up to 433 million cases of unintentional acute pesticide poisoning annually, affecting around 46% of agricultural workers worldwide. About 11,000 cases are fatal each year.
The burden falls disproportionately on the Global South, researchers found.
South and Southeast Asia and eastern Africa recorded the highest estimated numbers of cases. In Burkina Faso, nearly 84% of farmers are estimated to suffer acute pesticide poisoning each year.
“Behind these staggering numbers are farmers, workers and families paying a terrible human price for pesticide exposure,” PAN India Executive Director Jayakumar Chelaton said. “This research exposes a crisis that can no longer be ignored.”
The findings come as pesticides are increasingly used to protect food production, with global use more than doubling between 1990 and 2023, according to the study.
Without pesticides, between 20% and 40% of global crop yields could be lost to plant pests and diseases each year, according to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization.
The risks posed by pesticides add to wider food-security challenges, particularly in developing countries already struggling with climate shocks, conflict, and pressure on agricultural production. Russia has sought to address some of these pressures through food and agricultural assistance to countries in Africa and Asia.
Earlier this year, Moscow sent around 60 metric tons of emergency aid to cyclone-hit Madagascar and 29 metric tons of humanitarian supplies to Mozambique. In 2025, it donated more than 1,600 metric tons of grain to Ethiopia under an ongoing food assistance program. Russia also recently delivered 770 tons of food to Mali through the UN World Food Program (WFP), enough to support more than 57,000 vulnerable people for three months.
Russian companies have also provided fertilizer to countries facing food insecurity. Fertilizer producer Uralchem recently donated 30,000 metric tons of potash to Bangladesh in a shipment facilitated by the WFP. The company says it has donated more than 220,000 tons of mineral fertilizers free of charge since 2022, with shipments reaching Malawi, Kenya, Nigeria, Zimbabwe, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

'Enormous interest': Coalition says exiled crown prince of Iran will visit Australia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:05:54 UTC
13:05:54 KST

In Brief
- The exiled former crown prince of Iran has accepted an invitation from the Coalition to visit Australia.
- The Coalition says the invitation does not mean the party supports his bid to lead the country.
Six months after United States President Donald Trump attacked Iran and called for regime change in the country, the Coalition says the exiled crown prince of Iran will visit Australia at their invitation.
Reza Pahlavi is the son of the shah of Iran, who was ousted by the Islamic Revolution. Pahlavi has lived outside Iran since 1979, and has long advocated for the fall of the current regime, positioning himself as an alternative leader for the country.
In a statement, Opposition foreign affairs spokesperson Ted O'Brien said the party's invitation to Pahlavi was not an endorsement of his leadership in Iran.
"Iran's future belongs to the Iranian people. It is not for Australia to determine who should lead Iran or what form its future government should take," O'Brien said.
The statement said the Coalition was "responding to Iranian-Australians who want their voices heard".
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
"We should be prepared to listen to credible voices advocating for a peaceful and democratic alternative to the regime in Tehran."
The statement said Pahlavi had accepted the Coalition's invitation to visit Australia for the first time since 1978, before his father's regime was overthrown.
The details of this visit are yet to be finalised, but the statement said Coalition MPs and senators would meet "virtually" with the former crown prince in the coming weeks "to discuss the situation in Iran, the aspirations of the Iranian people and his advocacy for a democratic transition to a secular Iran".
Engagement with Australian-Iranians
In its statement, the Coalition said the invitation had come off the back of "enormous interest from the Iranian-Australian community".
"Thousands of Persian Australians have signed our petition to bring Reza Pahlavi to Australia, Liberal MP Julian Leeser said.
O'Brien said engagement with Iranian-Australians formed part of the Coalition's broader engagement with diaspora communities.
"For decades, the Iranian people have suffered under a brutal terrorist regime that represses its own citizens, exports terror abroad and denies its people basic freedoms."
Who is Reza Pahlavi?
After entering exile alongside his father Mohammad Reza Pahlavi — the last shah of Iran — Reza Pahlavi has become an avid supporter of opponents to Iran's ayatollahs.
Now living in the US, he has positioned himself as a person who could lead a secular, democratic Iran. He has seen his support soar in Iran and throughout the Iranian diaspora.
In January, domestic demonstrations against the regime gripped Iran, as protesters took to the streets in the thousands to protest the country's economic problems and the regime itself.
The government responded with a communications blackout and violent force against unarmed civilians. The Iranian government has said 3,100 protesters were killed during the blackout, but the United Nations has suggested the number could be as high as 20,000.
In response, Pahlavi called for a 'global day of action' in February, spurring thousands of people to rally in his support around the world.
Thousands gathered in Sydney, Melbourne, Perth and Brisbane.
Pahlavi himself addressed a 250,000-person rally in Munich.
Controversially, Pahlavi has actively advocated for foreign interference in Iran. He has also faced criticism from those who question whether someone who has not lived in Iran for 50 years can legitimately position himself as a possible leader for the country.
Trump himself has expressed this concern, and despite claiming to have waged war against Iran for a variety of reasons, including regime change, Trump does not endorse Pahlavi's bid to run the country.

Government offers small businesses a trust tax workaround
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:02:48 UTC
13:02:48 KST

Government offers small businesses a trust tax workaround
In short:
The federal government has proposed a workaround for small businesses who were worried about paying state stamp duties when they restructure out of discretionary trusts to avoid the proposed minimum tax.
They will instead be able to restructure their affairs without actually changing their trust structures, remaining exempt from the tax as long as they do not vary their distributions.
What's next?
The draft legislation is open for consultation for two weeks.
Small businesses could avoid being stung by stamp duty when they restructure to escape Labor's minimum tax on discretionary trusts, under a workaround proposed by Treasurer Jim Chalmers.
Draft laws to enact the 30 per cent trust tax were released for feedback on Thursday. The tax is the last of the major tax changes from the May federal budget to be legislated.
Fears about stamp duty had been raised with the government during consultation, with small business lobby COSBOA warning those who used discretionary trusts could be left with "an impossible choice between a higher tax burden or a costly restructure".
The workaround would allow trustees to avoid an official restructure, exempting them from the tax if they agreed to shift their existing beneficiaries to a fixed-income structure.
Why stamp duty loomed as an issue
Stamp duties are collected by states and territories when property is transferred or transacted.
Financial assets count as property, so small business restructures usually trigger stamp duty.
Many businesses were expected to restructure to avoid the new trust tax.
Labor's tax applies only to discretionary trusts, a type of financial vehicle which gives their owners flexibility to shift income between an array of companies and beneficiaries and across time.
The government has argued the trusts are used to minimise tax.
By restructuring into a company structure or a "fixed" trust, which doles out income in steady proportions, trustees would forfeit the flexibility benefits but avoid the new tax.
But doing so would be expensive. The budget papers promised "rollover relief" for "small businesses and others".
But similar federal rollover programs do not cover state stamp duties, applying to federal income taxes only.
How Labor is proposing to swerve the stamp duty issue
The government had indicated it wanted to fix the issue and sought ideas through the consultation process.
But state treasurers had responded with reluctance or even outright hostility to suggestions they may be asked to waive stamp duty.
This workaround is designed to avoid triggering a stamp duty event, effectively by allowing small business to keep their discretionary trusts, but opt out of actually using their discretion.
Rather than converting to a fixed trust and triggering stamp duty, the legislation would allow trustees to choose to make fixed distributions to their existing beneficiaries, making them exempt from the trust tax as long as they keep the fix in place.
Another change would exempt from the tax any donations made from discretionary trusts to registered charities, deductible gift recipients, or "income-tax exempt entities" such as religious groups or sporting clubs.
Some trustees had raised concerns that charitable giving would be discouraged without such an exemption.
The trust tax will begin in mid-2028, a year later than capital gains and negative gearing changes.
There are many exemptions, including for super funds, disability trusts, deceased estates, testamentary trusts, charitable trusts, and farm income.
Business groups have also called for help with the cost of legal and financial advice to restructure.
Andrew McKellar of business group ACCI said in July that these costs were "extensive … not to mention the serious costs in time and stress".
Consultation on the draft is open for two weeks, closing on September 18.

From Residual Land to Civic Places: 6 Mexican Public Parks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
04:00:00 UTC
13:00:00 KST

Mexico's rapid urban growth over recent decades has left many cities struggling with fragmented neighborhoods, high crime rates, and severe shortages of quality public spaces. In many low-income urban areas, informal development occurred alongside raw infrastructure like drainage canals, rail lines, and steep ravines, dividing communities and creating hazardous vacant zones. To address this spatial segregation and lack of civic amenities, public agencies and architects across Mexico are intervening in these abandoned buffer zones to construct public parks. By converting former physical barriers into accessible pedestrian corridors, these projects rejoin separated neighborhoods, re-establish safe visual sight lines, and provide spaces for community gathering and daily recreation.
To ensure these interventions survive harsh climate conditions and potential municipal maintenance neglect, architects rely on durable, low-cost construction strategies centered on integrally colored concrete and locally sourced materials. Poured concrete (often tinted with earth tones) is used for retainers, steps, climbing walls, and site furniture, providing structural stability and high wear resistance without needing regular repainting or specialized upkeep. These concrete structures are frequently combined with porous local gravels and recycled elements such as tire retaining walls to manage stormwater runoff and control soil erosion. By pairing long-lasting, heavy-duty materials with step-free accessibility and open layouts, these designs establish permanent civic infrastructure that remains functional for long-term public use.

Season uncertainty 'challenging' for AFLW community
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
03:57:51 UTC
12:57:51 KST

Uncertainty about AFLW key season dates has 'significant impact'
The 2026 men's AFL season is still being contested and we already know when next year's grand final is set to be.
Compare that to the AFLW, where this season's decider was announced just before the start of round three, 13 weeks before the date.
Key dates for the men's season are announced well in advance, with possible season start dates, Gather Round weekend and the grand final for next year already known to fans.
This gives clubs and players heading on their off-season breaks clarity when planning for personnel to return to the club. One benefit of this is being able to time pre-season training in order to be in peak condition when the season begins in March.
Former AFLW player and senior coach Lauren Arnell says more certainty would allow clubs to plan their pre-season to get the best performance out of the playing group.
"It's challenging when you don't have absolute security on that because one week more or less in your preseason has a significant impact on all planning, not just high performance, but on what you can educate as a footy program as well," Arnell told ABC Sport.
The AFLW grand final will be played on November 27, after a 12-round home and away season.
The AFLW grand-final announcement came at half time of the men's Wildcard final between Collingwood and the Western Bulldogs, which the league said was a deliberate decision to get more coverage of the announcement.
Despite this, the broadcast on Foxtel/Kayo did not mention the announcement in the half-time break.
Men's players have 196 days from the key dates announcement to March 17, the earliest proposed date for the 2027 season to begin, and 395 days until next year's season decider. At the time of writing there are still 23 days until the 2026 grand final.
In a statement from the AFL accompanying the release, CEO Andrew Dillon highlighted the need for fans and clubs to be informed ahead of time.
"We're really pleased to be able to provide fans and clubs with this clarity well ahead of the 2027 season," Dillon said.
The AFL announced the women's fixture on May 21 of this year, giving clubs 80 days' notice, less than half the time their male counterparts have to prepare for the season.
Many AFLW players are still working full-time jobs outside their football careers and Arnell says more certainty would benefit them as well.
"There are still players in the competition working day jobs, and so those players letting their employers know has become more and more challenging," she said.
Rebecca Miller, who plays for the Richmond Tigers AFLW side, says an earlier fixture would also allow the league more time to promote the competition to fans.
"There's been times we've gone to community camps early in preseason or we've done appearances at a men's game early in the season and people are like, 'When are you playing?' And you're like, 'I don't know. I don't have a draw' so you just feel a bit silly in that regard," Miller told ABC Sport.
Most AFL fans will know that the men's grand final is typically held in the last week of September and occasionally, like in 2027, in the first weekend of October. The AFLW grand final is yet to have that level of certainty, having been held in March, April, November and December across nine editions.
"It probably just goes back to that preparation; if we know the grand final, when and where it is before the season starts, again that marketing and promotion piece can really ramp up and make sure that our centrepiece is well attended and well watched and get the attendance they deserve," Miller said.
Conversely, the NRL announced its 2026 men's and women's fixtures on November 14, 2025, which gave NRLW clubs 230 days to prepare for their season to launch and allowed fans time to plan which games they want to attend the following season.
"They [the NRL] have the draw out for the men's and the women's team so at Christmas I can talk to my family about which games they're gonna go to and plan for it months in advance," Miller said, "to be able to go into the Christmas period and know your draw and be able to set yourself as a player but also as a fan and a member".
NRLW matches this year have had an average attendance of 4,915 after seven rounds. Round three of AFLW had an average crowd of 4,806 fans, which includes five double-headers with men's matches. If you count only standalone matches the average attendance is 2,293 for matches that provided a crowd number.
Miller believes that more notice would not just allow more time for promotion, it could also give players more motivation during a long preseason.
"It's so exciting and it just makes it all real. You circle a few games in particular from an individual point of view because you like playing that opposition or you have some beef against that opposition," she said.
"Your family and your friends can decide 'I want to come down to this game, come to that game' so it just makes it all real in your mind and you know why you're training, you know what you're training for".
Arnell believes the announcement of key dates is important but the next steps should come around fixturing.
"I think a priority for AFLW needs to be that all teams play each other once and then you start to land on where your season begins in a calendar and where your grand final sits," she said.

Unstable Tibetan Plateau risks cascading disasters as glacier losses mount in Nepal, China
Experts find downstream erosion is critical to scale of destruction as death toll continues to rise from China-Nepal landslide and floods
“Over the past 60 years, the glacier area on the Tibetan Plateau has shrunk by around 24 per cent, with around 7,000 small glaciers disappearing completely,” Gao Rong, deputy director of China’s National Climate Centre, said on Wednesday.
“Looking ahead, the structural stability of glaciers across the Tibetan Plateau will decline further. Glacial disasters are likely to become more frequent and could amplify in destruction and reach through cascading effects.”
Beijing has stepped up cross-border support to its neighbour. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said on Wednesday that China’s second batch of emergency supplies arrived in Kathmandu on Tuesday afternoon, accompanied by five DNA identification experts. A third shipment and a second expert team were being prepared.
After working for seven days, Beijing on Wednesday cleared the road to Gyirong Port, which was hit hardest on the Chinese side by the mudslide. Heavy machinery has reached the checkpoint area to aid a deeper search.
The mudslide created by the glacier collapse travelled 22km (13.7 miles) along the valley and reached the Gyirong Port border crossing in just seven minutes, according to an initial assessment last week.

Venezuela’s Maduro seeks dismissal of US charges, citing immunity
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
03:45:24 UTC
12:45:24 KST

Venezuela’s Maduro seeks dismissal of US charges, citing immunity
Nicolas Maduro’s lawyer says head-of-state immunity bars US prosecution over drug trafficking charges
Ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro urged a US judge on Wednesday to dismiss criminal drug trafficking charges against him, arguing he should be immune from prosecution as the head of a sovereign country.
The charges, filed in Manhattan federal court, formed the basis for the US military’s raid on Caracas and capture of Maduro on January 3. The Venezuelan leader, who has been held in a Brooklyn federal jail since his seizure, has pleaded not guilty and is scheduled to go on trial on June 1, 2027, if his effort to dismiss the case is unsuccessful.
The principle that sitting heads of state are immune from prosecution abroad is a long-standing tenet of international law seen as fundamental to diplomacy. Maduro’s push to persuade Manhattan-based US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein to dismiss the case will test US courts’ general reluctance to apply international law in criminal cases.
Maduro’s lawyer, Barry Pollack, made the assertion of immunity in a motion to dismiss Maduro’s indictment. Hellerstein had given Pollack a deadline of Wednesday to file the motion.
Pollack said Hellerstein lacked jurisdiction both because sovereign heads of state enjoyed complete immunity and because the acts that Maduro is accused of would have been part of his official duties.
“This unprecedented prosecution violates the absolute immunity from criminal jurisdiction to which heads of state and foreign officials acting in their official capacities have been entitled for hundreds of years,” Pollack wrote.

Military chaplain: Religious education helps build patriotism in armed forces
This is stated in an Ukrinform publication titled “He put aside the cross and took up a rifle.”
“Religious education helps promote military-patriotic values in modern armed forces. After all, one cannot love God without loving one’s homeland. A spiritually mature believer understands that they must defend their home and their country,” said Father Vasyl Borysevych, a chaplain with the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ 123rd Unmanned Systems Brigade Code of Orion.
According to him, during confessions and conversations, service members often ask how they should reconcile their military duties with God’s commandment, “Thou shalt not kill.” This is particularly relevant to deeply religious believers.
“They ask: ‘What am I supposed to do? I have broken one of the main commandments. Will I now burn in hell?’ We try to explain that in Scripture, the commandment ‘Thou shalt not kill’ does not apply to warriors. It refers to those who want to take someone’s life for some selfish purpose, for example, to seize another person’s property. But protecting your family and loved ones is different. The Gospel of John says: ‘Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends,’” the chaplain explained.
He stressed that no religious denomination prohibits military service. Many service members serve in the rear, provide logistical support, work as medics, prepare food, and perform other duties.
“It is another matter when people use their faith as a pretext for failing to fulfill their duty to defend their homeland. There are even such cases among clergy who are mobilized after five years of war and then complain that their rights are being violated,” the chaplain said.
As reported by Ukrinform, representatives of different religious denominations in the Ukrainian Armed Forces coexist harmoniously and demonstrate a high level of military brotherhood.

ADHD may have a surprising creative advantage
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
03:44:06 UTC
12:44:06 KST

ADHD may have a surprising creative advantage
The same wandering attention that can make ADHD difficult may also be a hidden engine for creativity.
- Date:
- September 2, 2026
- Source:
- Constructor University
- Summary:
- Some of the attention patterns that make ADHD challenging may also help spark creativity by allowing the brain to explore more ideas and unexpected connections. Researchers think creative activities could potentially channel this “defocused attention” while helping strengthen the brain systems involved in focus and self-control.
- Share:
ADHD affects millions of people and can make everyday tasks involving focus, impulse control, and sustained attention more difficult. At the same time, traits associated with ADHD are also found among highly successful artists and innovators, including Justin Timberlake and Simone Biles. New research from Constructor University neuroscientist Dr. Radwa Khalil examines the science behind this apparent contradiction.
Published in iScience, the research explores the neurological overlap between attention and creativity. It suggests that some mental processes linked to ADHD, including defocused attention, may also support creative thinking when they are directed in productive ways. The findings point to the possibility that creative activities such as art, music, and dance could eventually serve as non-pharmacological interventions for the nearly 8% of children worldwide affected by ADHD.
Rethinking ADHD Beyond Deficits
The study, co-authored by researchers from several prestigious French research institutions, reflects a broader effort to reconsider how ADHD is understood.
"There's a tendency to view attention-related conditions like ADHD purely through the lens of deficit: what is wrong, what is missing, or what needs to be fixed?" said Dr. Khalil.
Although ADHD is commonly approached as a disorder defined by difficulties, Khalil said emerging research shows that attention and creativity rely on some of the same neural networks.
"Neurodivergent attention patterns, then, are not merely problems. They can open pathways to powerful creative thinking when directed appropriately," she said.
The work, titled Attention Unleashed: creative therapy for thoughtful transformation, brings together findings from multiple research fields to show how the brain systems involved in attention also overlap with those involved in creativity.
The researchers highlight free-associative thought as one example of this connection. The ability to let ideas move in unexpected directions can contribute to creative insights, but similar patterns are also associated with distractibility, mind-wandering, and other behaviors frequently seen in ADHD.
ADHD and the Brain's Wider Spotlight
Khalil described the relationship using the image of a spotlight.
"Think of attention like a spotlight. Most people are able to focus their beam on one thing. ADHD brains have a wider spotlight, taking in more information at once. This condition can make routine tasks that require focus challenging. However, this broader view, or 'defocused attention', also encourages exploratory thinking and new idea combinations, which fuel creativity."
In other words, a broader attentional field can create difficulties when a task demands concentration on a single goal. But that same tendency to absorb more information and move among different ideas may encourage exploration and make it easier to form unexpected connections.
The Healing Power of Creativity
Khalil and her colleagues believe this connection could have practical implications for ADHD and related disorders.
Creative activities including art, music, dance, writing, gaming, and others may give people with ADHD structured ways to direct and explore defocused attention. The researchers also suggest that engaging in creative work could help strengthen neural networks involved in controlling attention, potentially reshaping patterns associated with impulsivity and hyperactivity.
"Authentic creative expression is so much more than a pleasant distraction," continued Dr. Khalil. "It is engaging the same neural circuits involved in attention control, essentially providing a workout for the brain. For a child with ADHD, the experience of getting 'lost in the moment' when creating art or playing music may actually be strengthening their ability to focus by working with their natural cognitive style instead of against it."
More Research Is Still Needed
Despite the potential, the researchers emphasize that scientists still do not fully understand the relationship between creativity and attention.
To help close those gaps, the study proposes a framework for future research. Its recommendations include greater interdisciplinary collaboration, new methodological approaches, and longitudinal studies that can track changes over time.
Khalil argues that any major shift in how ADHD is treated will require a broad research effort bringing together neuroscientists, art therapists, clinicians, and other specialists. Building that interdisciplinary foundation could help researchers determine when creative approaches are most useful and how they might eventually complement existing ADHD interventions.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Constructor University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Sarah Bou Sader Nehme, Emiliano Macaluso, Radwa Khalil. Attention unleashed: Creative therapy for thoughtful transformation. iScience, 2026; 29 (5): 115387 DOI: 10.1016/j.isci.2026.115387

Scientists find genes linked to OCD, raising the prospect of new treatments
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
03:40:00 UTC
12:40:00 KST

US scientists find genes linked to OCD, raising the prospect of new treatments
NEW YORK – Researchers have identified 36 genes that substantially raise the risk for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and chronic tic disorders, a discovery that could lead to new treatments.
OCD is characterised by persistent intrusive thoughts and repetitive behaviours, while chronic tic disorders, including Tourette syndrome, involve sudden, repeated movements or vocalisations that are difficult to control.
“In the past, we knew about a couple of strong genes, so there were few opportunities for the pharmaceutical industry to develop drugs,” co-author Jay Tischfield, an emeritus distinguished professor in New Jersey’s Rutgers School of Arts and Sciences, said in a statement.
“Now you’ve got over 30 targets, and that opens up new possibilities for treatment development.”
The study, published on Sept 1 in Nature Neuroscience, analysed DNA from nearly 4,000 people diagnosed with these conditions.
Many of the newly identified genes are shared between OCD and chronic tic disorders. 
At the biological level, the disorders appear to involve many of the same brain pathways, the researchers found.
“These genes don’t act individually,” said Tischfield. “They act in networks. And now you can target whole networks, which will make it easier to design new therapies.”
The researchers also found that several of the identified genes were previously linked to autism and schizophrenia, reinforcing increasing evidence that multiple psychiatric conditions may stem from related disruptions in brain development and communication.
Brain cells communicate using chemical signals called neurotransmitters that carry messages from one nerve cell to another. The genes identified in the study appear to influence how those signals move through the brain’s circuitry.
By revealing the biological systems behind the disorders, the findings could aid the design of drugs that target the underlying mechanisms rather than simply managing symptoms, the researchers said.
Blocking a protein may help prevent fatty liver injuries
A protein inside the “energy factories” of liver cells appears to trigger the damage seen in some patients with fatty liver disease, researchers have discovered.
Obesity-related liver disease affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide, but only a fraction of those livers develop scarring, become inflamed and eventually fail, the researchers noted in a report published on Sept 1 in the Journal Of Clinical Investigation.
EFHD1, a calcium-binding protein in the membrane of the mitochondria, drives that process, they found. Blocking it protects against liver injury in human cells and in mice consuming a high-fat diet.
Using biochemical and imaging tests, the team found that EFHD1 tethers mitochondria to a nearby organelle called the endoplasmic reticulum and helps trigger mitochondrial division.
When mice are fed a fatty, sugary diet, excess lipids drive up EFHD1 levels, which makes the mitochondria divide so much that they start leaking their contents into the rest of the cell. 
Those contents include double-stranded RNA, which can also appear in the presence of certain viruses, like hepatitis C. Upon detecting the double-stranded RNA, the cell activates an antiviral defence pathway.
That response, meant to prevent viral replication in infected cells, instead shuts down healthy liver cells, worsening injury, according to the researchers.
When the researchers blocked or reduced the levels of EFHD1, measures of inflammation and liver scarring dropped by roughly 30 per cent to 60 per cent in mice with liver injuries resulting from diet or drug treatments and in miniature models of human livers in test tubes.
The researchers also found that mice engineered to lack EFHD1 have normal activity levels, weight gain and other measures of metabolism, which suggests that treatments that block EFHD1 may have few side effects. They said they are currently working to develop such a drug.
“This research may help people by identifying new biological pathways which can be targeted with drugs to help stave off liver disease by limiting how fat build-up damages the liver,” study leader David Eberhardt of University of Utah Health said in a statement. REUTERS
